title.zh: 卷六十三 列傳第十三: 封倫 蕭瑀 裴矩 宇文士及
title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 13: Feng Lun, Xiao Yu, Pei Ju, Yuwen Shiji
title.raw: 卷六十三 列傳第十三: 封倫 蕭瑀 裴矩 宇文士及 Volume 63 Biographies 13: Feng Lun, Xiao Yu, Pei Ju, Yuwen Shiji

sentences.zh: 封倫 倫子言道 兄子行高

translations.literal: Feng Lun; his son Yan Dao; his elder brother's son Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun; his son Yan Dao; and his brother's son Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀 子銳 兄子鈞 鈞子瓘 鈞兄子嗣業裴矩 矩子宣機

translations.literal: Xiao Yu; his son Rui; his elder brother's son Jun; Jun's son Zan; Jun's elder brother's son Siye; Pei Ju; Ju's son Xuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu; his son Rui; his brother's son Jun; Jun's son Zan; Jun's brother's son Siye; Pei Ju; and Ju's son Xuanji.

sentences.zh: 宇文士及

translations.literal: Yuwen Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shiji.

sentences.zh: 封倫，字德彝，觀州蓚人。

translations.literal: Feng Lun, whose courtesy name was Deyi, was a native of Lou in Guan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun, courtesy name Deyi, came from Lou in Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 北齊太子太保隆之孫。

translations.literal: He was the grandson of Long, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was the grandson of Long, who had served as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父子繡，隋通州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zixiu was Prefect of Tong Prefecture under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zixiu had been prefect of Tong Prefecture in Sui times.

sentences.zh: 倫少時，其舅盧思道每言曰：「此子智識過人，必能致位卿相。

translations.literal: When Lun was young, his maternal uncle Lu Sidao often said, "This boy's intelligence surpasses others; he will surely attain the rank of chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Lun's maternal uncle Lu Sidao would often say, "This boy's mind outstrips other men's; he is sure to rise to ministerial rank."

sentences.zh: 」開皇末，江南作亂，內史令楊素往征之，署為行軍記室。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era, rebellion broke out in Jiangnan; Interior Minister Yang Su went to suppress it and appointed him army record-keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Kaihuang reign, when the south rose in revolt, Interior Minister Yang Su marched to suppress it and made Lun his campaign record-keeper.

sentences.zh: 船至海曲，素召之，倫墜於水中，人救免溺，乃易衣以見，竟寢不言。

translations.literal: When the ship reached Haiqu, Su summoned him; Lun fell into the water, was rescued from drowning, changed clothes to appear, and in the end kept silent and did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the fleet reached Haiqu, Su sent for him; Lun had fallen overboard and was pulled out before he drowned, then changed clothes and came to audience—yet he never mentioned the incident.

sentences.zh: 素後知，問其故，曰：「私事也，所以不白。

translations.literal: Su later learned of it and asked the reason; he said, "It was a private matter, and therefore I did not report it."
translations.idiomatic: When Su later found out and asked why, Lun replied, "It was a private affair, which is why I did not report it."

sentences.zh: 」素甚嗟異之。

translations.literal: Su greatly sighed in admiration at this.
translations.idiomatic: Su was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 素將營仁壽宮，引為土木監。

translations.literal: When Su was about to build Renshou Palace, he brought him in as overseer of earthworks and timber.
translations.idiomatic: When Su undertook construction of Renshou Palace, he appointed Lun overseer of the building works.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝至宮所，見制度奢侈，大怒曰：「楊素為不誠矣！

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui arrived at the palace site and saw the regulations were extravagant, he said in great anger, "Yang Su has been dishonest!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen visited the site and saw how lavish the design was, he flew into a rage: "Yang Su has deceived me!"

sentences.zh: 殫百姓之力，雕飾離宮，為吾結怨於天下。

translations.literal: He has exhausted the strength of the common people and ornamented a detached palace, bringing resentment upon me throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He has drained the people's strength to adorn a pleasure palace and has made the whole realm resent me.

sentences.zh: 」素惶恐，慮將獲譴。

translations.literal: Su was fearful and apprehensive that he would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Su was terrified, fearing he would be punished.

sentences.zh: 倫曰：「公當弗憂，待皇后至，必有恩詔。

translations.literal: Lun said, "Your Excellency should not worry; when the empress arrives there will surely be an edict of grace."
translations.idiomatic: Lun said, "Do not worry, sir—once the empress comes, you are sure to receive a gracious edict."

sentences.zh: 」明日，果召素入對，獨狐後勞之曰：「公知吾夫妻年老，無以娛心，盛飾此宮，豈非孝順。

translations.literal: The next day, Su was indeed summoned for audience; Empress Dugu comforted him, saying, "Your Excellency knows that we husband and wife are old and have nothing to delight our hearts; to adorn this palace splendidly—is this not filial piety?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Su was summoned as Lun had predicted; Empress Dugu reassured him: "You know we are old and need diversion; to lavish ornament on this palace—is that not filial devotion?"

sentences.zh: 」素退問倫曰：「卿何以知之？

translations.literal: When Su withdrew he asked Lun, "How did you know?"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Su asked Lun, "How did you know?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「至尊性儉，故初見而怒，然雅聽後言。

translations.literal: He replied, "His Majesty is by nature frugal, and therefore was angry at first sight; yet he is accustomed to heed what is said afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Lun answered, "The Son of Heaven is frugal by nature, so his first glance provoked anger—but he is used to listening to what comes after."

sentences.zh: 後，婦人也，惟麗是好，後心既悅，帝慮必移，所以知耳。

translations.literal: The empress is a woman and loves only splendor; once her heart is pleased, the emperor's mind is sure to shift—that is how I knew."
translations.idiomatic: The empress is a woman who loves beauty alone; once she is pleased, the emperor's concern will surely ease—that is why I knew."

sentences.zh: 」素嘆伏曰：「揣摩之才，非吾所及。

translations.literal: Su sighed in submission and said, "Talent for reading minds—this is not something I can match."
translations.idiomatic: Su sighed in admiration: "Your gift for reading people's hearts is beyond me."

sentences.zh: 」素負貴恃才，多所凌侮，唯擊賞倫。

translations.literal: Su, relying on his nobility and talent, often insulted others, but only prized and admired Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Su, proud of his rank and talent, bullied many men—yet he prized Lun alone.

sentences.zh: 每引與論宰相之務，終日忘倦，因撫其床曰：「封郎必當據吾此座。

translations.literal: He would often draw him in to discuss the duties of a chief minister, forgetting weariness all day, and patting his couch said, "Master Feng will surely occupy this seat of mine."
translations.idiomatic: He often drew Lun into talks on the chancellor's duties and would forget fatigue for a whole day; once, patting his own couch, he said, "Young Feng will surely sit in this place of mine."

sentences.zh: 」驟稱薦於文帝，由是擢授內史舍人。

translations.literal: He repeatedly praised and recommended him to Emperor Wen, and thereby Lun was promoted and appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly commended Lun to Emperor Wen, who thereupon promoted him to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 大業中，倫見虞世基幸於煬帝而不閒吏務，每有承受，多失事機。

translations.literal: During the Daye era, Lun saw that Yu Shiji was favored by Emperor Yang yet was unskilled in official business; whenever he received matters, he often missed the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign Lun saw Yu Shiji favored by Emperor Yang but negligent of administration; whenever business came to him, he often let the moment slip.

sentences.zh: 倫又托附之，密為指畫，宣行詔命，諂順主心。

translations.literal: Lun also attached himself to him, secretly giving guidance, promulgating edicts, and flattering to suit the sovereign's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Lun also attached himself to Yu, secretly directing policy, issuing edicts in his name, and flattering whatever pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 外有表疏如忤意者，皆寢而不奏。

translations.literal: Whenever memorials from outside seemed to offend the emperor's intent, they were all shelved and not presented.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from outside that seemed to displease the throne were all suppressed and never forwarded.

sentences.zh: 決斷刑法，多峻文深誣；

translations.literal: In deciding penal law, there were many harsh statutes and deep false accusations;
translations.idiomatic: Penal decisions leaned toward harsh statutes and deep false charges;

sentences.zh: 策勳行賞，必抑削之。

translations.literal: when planning merit and bestowing rewards, they were always reduced and cut back.
translations.idiomatic: and when merit was assessed and rewards granted, they were always pared down.

sentences.zh: 故世基之寵日隆，而隋政日壞，皆倫所為也。

translations.literal: Therefore Yu's favor grew daily while Sui government daily worsened—all was Lun's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yu's favor rose day by day while Sui governance rotted—and Lun was behind it all.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之亂，逼帝出宮，使倫數帝之罪。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Yuwen Huaji, the emperor was forced from the palace and Lun was made to enumerate the emperor's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuwen Huaji's revolt the emperor was driven from the palace and Lun was ordered to recite his crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「卿是士人，何至於此？

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "You are a gentleman—how could you come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are a scholar—how could you sink to this?"

sentences.zh: 」倫赧然而退。

translations.literal: Lun withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Lun withdrew, flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 化及尋署內史令，從至聊城。

translations.literal: Huaji soon appointed him Interior Minister and he followed him to Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji soon made him interior minister and Lun followed him to Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 倫見化及勢蹙，乃潛結化及弟士及，請於濟北運糧，以觀其變。

translations.literal: Lun saw that Huaji's position was desperate; he secretly allied with Huaji's younger brother Shiji and requested to transport grain in Jibei to watch how events would change.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Huaji's cause failing, Lun secretly aligned with Huaji's brother Shiji and asked leave to haul grain in Jibei so he could watch how fortunes turned.

sentences.zh: 遇化及敗，與士及來降。

translations.literal: When Huaji was defeated, he came to surrender together with Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji fell, he came over with Shiji to surrender.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其前代舊臣，遣使迎勞，拜內史舍人。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because he was an old minister of the previous dynasty, sent envoys to welcome and comfort him and appointed him Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, treating him as a veteran of the former dynasty, sent envoys to welcome him and appointed him Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 尋遷內史侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗幸溫湯，經秦始皇墓，謂倫曰：「古者帝王，竭生靈之力，殫府庫之財，營起山陵，此復何益？

translations.literal: Gaozu once visited the hot springs and passed the tomb of the First Emperor of Qin; he said to Lun, "In antiquity emperors exhausted the strength of the living and depleted the treasury to build mountain tombs—what further use is there in this?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, on his way to the hot springs, Gaozu passed Qin Shihuang's tomb and asked Lun, "Ancient emperors drained the people's strength and emptied the treasury to raise great burial mounds—what good did it do?"

sentences.zh: 」倫曰：「上之化下，猶風之靡草。

translations.literal: Lun said, "The superior transforming the inferior is like wind bending grass."
translations.idiomatic: Lun replied, "When those above set the tone, those below follow—as grass bends in the wind."

sentences.zh: 自秦、漢帝王盛為厚葬，故百官眾庶競相遵仿。

translations.literal: Since Qin and Han emperors made lavish burial the fashion, officials and commoners all vied to follow the example.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Qin and Han rulers lavished wealth on tombs, officials and commoners have rushed to imitate them.

sentences.zh: 凡是古冢丘封，悉多藏珍寶，咸見開發。

translations.literal: As for all ancient mounds and sealed tombs, most hoarded treasures and have all been opened.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly every ancient mound was stuffed with treasure—and nearly every one has been looted.

sentences.zh: 若死而無知，厚葬深為虛費；

translations.literal: If the dead have no awareness, lavish burial is deeply a vain waste;
translations.idiomatic: If the dead feel nothing, lavish burial is pure waste;

sentences.zh: 若魂而有識，被髮豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: if the soul has awareness, would not disheveled hair be agonizing!
translations.idiomatic: if the soul still knows, would it not writhe in anguish at its violated grave!"

sentences.zh: 」高祖稱善，謂倫曰：「從今之後，宜自上導下，悉為薄葬。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised this and said to Lun, "From now on we should guide those below from above and all practice simple burial."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu approved and told Lun, "Hereafter we must lead from the top and require simple burials throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 」太宗之討王世充，詔倫參謀軍事。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Wang Shichong, Lun was ordered to advise on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong marched against Wang Shichong, Lun was ordered to serve on his staff.

sentences.zh: 高祖以兵久在外，意欲旋師，太宗遣倫入朝親論事勢。

translations.literal: Because the army had long been abroad, Gaozu wished to withdraw; Taizong sent Lun to court to discuss the situation in person.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, weary of keeping troops in the field, meant to recall the army; Taizong sent Lun to court to argue the situation face to face.

sentences.zh: 倫言於高祖曰：「世充得地雖多，而羈縻相屬，其所用命者，唯洛陽一城而已，計盡力窮，破在朝夕。

translations.literal: Lun said to Gaozu, "Although Shichong has gained much territory, his holdings are only loosely tied together; the only place that truly obeys him is the single city of Luoyang. His plans are exhausted and his strength spent—his defeat is a matter of days."
translations.idiomatic: Lun told Gaozu, "Shichong may hold wide lands, but they hang together only loosely; only Luoyang truly answers his call. His schemes are spent and his strength gone—his fall is only a matter of days."

sentences.zh: 今若還兵，賊勢必振，更相連結，後必難圖。

translations.literal: If the army withdraws now, the rebels' momentum will surely revive; they will link up again, and later they will be hard to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw now and the rebels will rally and knit their forces together—then they will be far harder to crush."

sentences.zh: 未若乘其已衰，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Better to strike while they are already weakened—then breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike while they are already failing—then victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 」高祖納之。

translations.literal: Gaozu accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took his advice.

sentences.zh: 及太宗凱旋，高祖謂侍臣曰：「朕初發兵東討，眾議多有不同，唯秦王請行，封倫贊成此計。

translations.literal: When Taizong returned in triumph, Gaozu said to the attending ministers, "When I first sent troops east to attack, many in council disagreed; only the Prince of Qin asked to go, and Feng Lun supported this plan."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong returned victorious, Gaozu told his ministers, "When I first marched east, most at court dissented—only the Prince of Qin urged the campaign, and Feng Lun backed him."

sentences.zh: 昔張華協同晉武，亦復何以加也！

translations.literal: In former times Zhang Hua aided Emperor Wu of Jin—how could one add to that!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua once stood with Emperor Wu of Jin—what could surpass that!"

sentences.zh: 」封平原縣公，兼天冊府司馬。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan County and concurrently made Marshal of the Celestial Register Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Duke of Pingyuan and concurrently marshal of the Celestial Register Office.

sentences.zh: 會突厥寇太原，復遣使來請和親，高祖問群臣：「和之與戰，策將安出？

translations.literal: When the Turks raided Taiyuan and again sent envoys requesting marriage alliance, Gaozu asked the ministers, "Peace or war—which policy should we adopt?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided Taiyuan and again asked for a marriage alliance, Gaozu asked his ministers, "Peace or war—what course should we take?"

sentences.zh: 」多言戰則怨深，不如先和。

translations.literal: Most said that fighting would deepen resentment and it was better to make peace first.
translations.idiomatic: Most argued that war would only deepen hatred and that peace should come first.

sentences.zh: 倫曰：「突厥憑凌，有輕中國之意，必謂兵弱而不能戰。

translations.literal: Lun said, "The Turks rely on their arrogance and hold China in light esteem; they surely think our forces are weak and cannot fight."
translations.idiomatic: Lun said, "The Turks are overbearing and despise China—they will assume our armies are too weak to fight."

sentences.zh: 如臣計者，莫若悉眾以擊之，其勢必捷，勝而後和，恩威兼著。

translations.literal: By my plan, nothing is better than gathering all forces to strike them—the outcome will surely be swift victory; make peace only after winning, and both grace and awe will be manifest.
translations.idiomatic: In my view we should muster every soldier and strike—victory will come quickly; make peace only after we win, and both kindness and awe will be clear."

sentences.zh: 若今歲不戰，明年必當復來，臣以擊之為便。

translations.literal: If we do not fight this year, they will surely come again next year; I consider striking them the advantageous course.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not fight this year, they will be back next—striking now is the wiser course."

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之。

translations.literal: Gaozu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 六年，以本官檢校吏部尚書，曉習吏職，甚獲當時之譽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made acting Minister of Personnel while retaining his former office; skilled in official duties, he won great praise at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made acting minister of personnel while keeping his prior post; versed in bureaucratic business, he won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 八年，進封道國公，尋徙封於密。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to Duke of Daoguo and soon transferred his fief to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was raised to Duke of Daoguo, then soon had his fief moved to Mi.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀嘗薦倫於高祖，高祖任倫為中書令。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu once recommended Lun to Gaozu, and Gaozu appointed Lun Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu had once recommended Lun to Gaozu, who made him director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，瑀遷尚書左僕射，倫為右僕射。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Yu was moved to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Lun became Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Yu became left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and Lun the right vice director.

sentences.zh: 倫素險诐，與瑀商量可奏者，至太宗前，盡變易之，由是與瑀有隙。

translations.literal: Lun was by nature treacherous and deceitful; whatever he and Yu agreed could be submitted, once before Taizong he changed it all, and thereby he had a rift with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was treacherous by nature: matters he and Yu had settled to present, he altered entirely before Taizong—hence the breach between them.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，遘疾於尚書省，太宗親自臨視，即命尚輦送還第，尋薨，年六十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he fell ill at the Department of State Affairs; Taizong personally visited him, immediately ordered the imperial carriage to return him to his residence, and soon he died at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 he fell ill at the Department of State Affairs; Taizong visited him in person, ordered the imperial carriage to take him home, and he soon died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 太宗深悼之，廢朝三日，冊贈司空，謚曰明。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply mourned him, suspended court for three days, and by patent posthumously enfeoffed him as Minister of Works with the posthumous title Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him deeply, suspended court for three days, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Minister of Works with the posthumous name Ming.

sentences.zh: 初，倫數從太宗征討，特蒙顧遇。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lun had repeatedly followed Taizong on campaigns and received special favor and regard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lun had often followed Taizong on campaign and enjoyed his special favor.

sentences.zh: 以建成、元吉之故，數進忠款，太宗以為至誠，前後賞賜以萬計。

translations.literal: Because of Chengjian and Yuanji, he repeatedly offered loyal pledges; Taizong considered him utterly sincere, and rewards before and after numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the rivalry with Chengjian and Yuanji, he repeatedly professed loyalty; Taizong took him for utterly sincere and rewarded him lavishly time and again.

sentences.zh: 而倫潛持兩端，陰附建成。

translations.literal: Yet Lun secretly kept two sides and covertly attached himself to Chengjian.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lun secretly played both sides and quietly backed Chengjian.

sentences.zh: 時高祖將行廢立，猶豫未決，謀之於倫，倫固諫而止。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was about to carry out deposition and establishment but hesitated and had not decided; he consulted Lun, and Lun firmly remonstrated until he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was weighing deposition and succession but could not decide, he consulted Lun, who remonstrated so firmly that Gaozu abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 然所為秘隱，時人莫知，事具《建成傳》。

translations.literal: Yet what he did was secret and hidden, and people of the time did not know; the matter is given in full in the biography of Chengjian.
translations.idiomatic: What he did stayed hidden—no one at the time knew—and the full account appears in Chengjian's biography.

sentences.zh: 卒後數年，太宗方知其事。

translations.literal: Several years after his death Taizong finally learned of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Only years after Lun's death did Taizong learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 十七年，治書侍御史唐臨追劾倫曰：「臣聞事君之義，盡命不渝；

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Investigating Censor Tang Lin pursued impeachment of Lun, saying, "I have heard that the duty of serving one's lord is to give one's life without wavering;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Investigating Censor Tang Lin pursued charges against Lun, saying, "I have heard that serving one's lord means giving one's life without wavering;

sentences.zh: 為臣之節，歲寒無貳。

translations.literal: the integrity of a minister is to have no second loyalty in the cold of winter.
translations.idiomatic: a minister's integrity holds firm when the year turns cold.

sentences.zh: 苟虧其道，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: If one falls short of this Way, the crime cannot be contained by execution.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever betrays that duty deserves death without mercy.

sentences.zh: 倫位望鼎司，恩隆胙土，無心報效，乃肆奸謀，熒惑儲籓，獎成元惡，置於常典，理合誅夷。

translations.literal: Lun's position and reputation were of the highest office, his grace extended to fief lands; he had no heart to repay favor but instead indulged wicked plots, deluded the heir's establishment, and abetted the chief villain—by ordinary statutes he ought to have been exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Lun stood at the summit of office and had been showered with fiefs, yet he repaid no loyalty and instead plotted treachery, misled the heir, and abetted the arch-villain—by ordinary law he should have been executed to the last man.

sentences.zh: 但苞藏之狀，死而後發，猥加褒贈，未正嚴科。

translations.literal: Yet the hidden conduct emerged only after death, and he was vulgarly given posthumous honors without applying the severe penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his treachery surfaced only after death, and he was lavishly honored posthumously without proper punishment.

sentences.zh: 罪惡既彰，宜加貶黜，豈可仍疇爵邑，尚列台槐！

translations.literal: Now that his crimes are manifest, he should be further degraded and demoted—how can he still retain noble rank and fief, still stand among the ministers at court!
translations.idiomatic: His guilt is now plain—he should be degraded. How can his titles and fiefs stand, or his name remain among the great ministers!

sentences.zh: 此而不懲，將何沮勸？

translations.literal: If this is not punished, what will deter and encourage others?
translations.idiomatic: If this goes unpunished, what lesson will anyone draw?"

sentences.zh: 」太宗令百官詳議，民部尚書唐儉等議：「倫罪暴身後，恩結生前，所歷眾官，不可追奪，請降贈改謚。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered all officials to deliberate in detail; Minister of Revenue Tang Jian and others argued, "Lun's crimes were exposed after death, but favor was bound while he lived; the offices he held cannot be retroactively stripped—we ask only to reduce posthumous honors and change his posthumous title."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered a full deliberation. Minister of Revenue Tang Jian and others argued, "Lun's crimes appeared only after death, but favors were given in life—the offices he held cannot be clawed back; we ask only to reduce his posthumous honors and change his posthumous name."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之，於是改謚繆，黜其贈官，削所食實封。

translations.literal: An edict followed this; thereupon his posthumous title was changed to Miu, his posthumous office was removed, and the substantive fief he had received was cut.
translations.idiomatic: The edict agreed: his posthumous name became Miu, his posthumous office was revoked, and his substantive fief was stripped.

sentences.zh: 子言道，尚高祖女淮南長公主，官至宋州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yan Dao married Gaozu's daughter, the Princess Chang of Huainan, and reached the office of Prefect of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan Dao married Gaozu's daughter, Princess Chang of Huainan, and rose to prefect of Song.

sentences.zh: 倫兄子行高，以文學知名。

translations.literal: Lun's elder brother's son Xing Gao was renowned for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's nephew Xing Gao was known for his literary accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，官至禮部郎中。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he reached the office of Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he rose to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀，字時文。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu, whose courtesy name was Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, courtesy name Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 高祖梁武帝，曾祖昭明太子，祖察，後樑宣帝。

translations.literal: His founding ancestor was Emperor Wu of Liang; his great-grandfather was the Crown Prince Zhaoming; his grandfather was Cha, and his father was Emperor Xuan of Later Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He descended from Emperor Wu of Liang; his great-grandfather was Crown Prince Zhaoming; his grandfather was Xiao Cha; his father was Emperor Xuan of Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 父巋，明帝。

translations.literal: His father Kui was Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui was Emperor Ming of Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 瑀年九歲，封新安郡王，幼以孝行聞。

translations.literal: At age nine Yu was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an Commandery and in youth was known for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he was made Prince of Xin'an and was known from childhood for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 姊為隋晉王妃，從入長安。

translations.literal: His elder sister was consort to the Prince of Jin of Sui and followed him into Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister became consort to Sui's Prince of Jin and followed the court to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 聚學屬文，端正鯁亮。

translations.literal: He gathered learning and composed writings, upright and sternly bright.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to study and composition, bearing himself with upright, unyielding clarity.

sentences.zh: 好釋氏，常修梵行，每與沙門難及苦空，必詣微旨。

translations.literal: He favored Buddhism, often practiced Buddhist discipline, and whenever he debated with monks on suffering and emptiness he always reached the subtle meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Buddhism, kept Buddhist discipline, and whenever he debated monks on suffering and emptiness he pressed to the heart of the doctrine.

sentences.zh: 常觀劉孝標《辯命論》，惡其傷先王之教，迷性命之理，乃作《非辯命論》以釋之。

translations.literal: He often read Liu Xiaobiao's "Discourse on Fate" and hated that it harmed the teaching of the former kings and obscured the principle of nature and life; he therefore wrote "Against the Discourse on Fate" to refute it.
translations.idiomatic: He often read Liu Xiaobiao's Discourse on Fate and disliked how it undermined the sages' teaching and blurred the truth of life and fate; he wrote Against the Discourse on Fate to answer it.

sentences.zh: 大旨以為：「人稟天地以生，孰雲非命，然吉凶禍福，亦因人而有，若一之於命，其蔽已甚。

translations.literal: Its main purport was: "Human beings receive life from Heaven and Earth—who says there is no fate? Yet fortune and misfortune also arise through human action; to attribute everything to fate alone is a grave error."
translations.idiomatic: Its main argument ran: "We receive life from Heaven and Earth—who denies fate? Yet fortune and misfortune also depend on what people do; to blame everything on fate alone is a grave mistake."

sentences.zh: 」時晉府學士柳顧言、諸葛穎見而稱之曰：「自孝標後數十年間，言性命之理者，莫能詆詰。

translations.literal: At the time the academicians of the Jin establishment, Liu Guyan and Zhuge Ying, saw it and praised it, saying, "For several decades since Xiaobiao, none who spoke on the principle of nature and life could be refuted."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin palace scholars Liu Guyan and Zhuge Ying read it and said, "For decades since Xiaobiao, no one who wrote on fate and life could be answered—"

sentences.zh: 今蕭君此論，足療劉子膏肓。

translations.literal: Now Master Xiao's discourse is sufficient to cure Liu's deep-seated malady."
translations.idiomatic: but Master Xiao's essay is enough to cure Liu's disease in its marrow."

sentences.zh: 」煬帝為太子也，授太子右千牛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was heir apparent, Yu was appointed Right Thousand-Bull of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Di was crown prince, Yu was made Right Thousand-Bull in his household.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，遷尚衣奉御，檢校左翊衛鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Yu was moved to Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe and made acting Eagle-Flight Commander of the Left Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Yu became attendant of the imperial wardrobe and acting Eagle-Flight commander of the Left Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 忽遇風疾，命家人不即醫療，仍云：「若天假餘年，因此望為棲遁之資耳。

translations.literal: He suddenly suffered a wind ailment and ordered his household not to treat him immediately, still saying, "If Heaven grants me more years, I hope by this to gain the means to dwell in seclusion."
translations.idiomatic: He suddenly fell ill with a wind disorder and told his family not to treat him at once, saying, "If Heaven grants me more years, I mean to use this as my excuse to live in seclusion."

sentences.zh: 」蕭後聞而誨之：「以爾才智，足堪揚名顯親，豈得輕毀形骸而求隱逸？

translations.literal: When Empress Xiao heard this she admonished him: "With your talent and intelligence you are fully able to make a name and bring honor to your kin—how can you lightly ruin your body to seek reclusion?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiao heard and rebuked him: "With your gifts you could bring honor to your house—how can you neglect your health to chase reclusion?"

sentences.zh: 若以此致譴，則罪在不測。

translations.literal: If you bring reproof upon yourself for this, the offense is beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: If you bring punishment on yourself for this, the offense is beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 」病且愈，其姊勸勉之，故復有仕進志。

translations.literal: When his illness was nearly cured, his elder sister urged and encouraged him, and he again had the will to advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: As he recovered, his elder sister urged him on, and he again wished to pursue office.

sentences.zh: 累加銀青光祿大夫、內史侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Silver-Glittering Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Silver-Glittering Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既以後弟之親，委之機務，後數以言忤旨，漸見疏斥。

translations.literal: Because he was kin to the empress through her younger brother, he was entrusted with crucial affairs; the empress several times spoke against the emperor's intent and he was gradually distanced and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress's brother-in-law he was entrusted with weighty affairs, but the empress often spoke against the emperor's wishes and he was gradually pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 煬帝至雁門，為突厥所圍，瑀進謀曰：「如聞始畢托校獵至此，義成公主初不知其有違背之心。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang reached Yanmen and was besieged by the Turks, Yu offered a plan: "I hear that Shibi, under the pretext of a hunting expedition, has come here, and Princess Yicheng at first did not know he had rebellious intent."
translations.idiomatic: At Yanmen, besieged by the Turks, Yu proposed: "I hear Shibi has come here under the guise of a hunt, and Princess Yicheng may not yet know he means rebellion."

sentences.zh: 且北蕃夷俗，可賀敦知兵馬事。

translations.literal: Moreover, in northern barbarian custom the Khatun understands military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Among the northern tribes, moreover, the khatun often controls the armies.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖解平城之圍，乃是閼氏之力。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Gaozu of Han broke the siege of Pingcheng through the power of the Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Gaozu of Han broke the siege at Pingcheng through the Yanzhi's intervention.

sentences.zh: 況義成以帝女為妻，必恃大國之援。

translations.literal: Moreover Yicheng, as the emperor's daughter in marriage, surely relies on aid from the great state.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng, moreover, is an emperor's daughter by marriage—she will surely lean on our great power.

sentences.zh: 若發一單使以告義成，假使無益，事亦無損。

translations.literal: If we send a single envoy to inform Yicheng, even if it is of no benefit, the affair will also suffer no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Send a lone envoy to warn Yicheng—even if it fails, we lose nothing."

sentences.zh: 臣又竊聽輿人之誦，乃慮陛下平突厥後更事遼東，所以人心不一，或致挫敗。

translations.literal: I have also secretly listened to the common people's talk and fear that after Your Majesty pacifies the Turks you will again campaign against Liaodong; therefore hearts are not united and defeat may result.
translations.idiomatic: I have also overheard the people's talk—they fear that after the Turks are beaten you will march on Liaodong again; morale is divided and defeat may follow."

sentences.zh: 請下明詔告軍中，赦高麗而專攻突厥，則百姓心安，人自為戰。

translations.literal: I ask that a clear edict be issued to the army, pardoning Goguryeo and concentrating the attack on the Turks; then the people will be at ease and each man will fight of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Issue a clear edict to the army: pardon Goguryeo and fight the Turks alone—then the people will be reassured and every soldier will fight willingly."

sentences.zh: 」煬帝從之，於是發使詣可賀敦諭旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang followed this, and thereupon sent envoys to the Khatun to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Di agreed and sent envoys to the khatun with the imperial message.

sentences.zh: 俄而突厥解圍去，於後獲其諜人，云：義成公主遣使告急於始畢，稱北方有警，由是突厥解圍，蓋公主之助也。

translations.literal: Soon the Turks lifted the siege and departed; afterward a spy was captured who said Princess Yicheng had sent envoys in urgent appeal to Shibi, claiming there was alarm in the north—thereby the Turks raised the siege; it was the princess's aid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Turks lifted the siege. Later a spy revealed that Princess Yicheng had urgently warned Shibi of trouble in the north—thus the siege ended, thanks to the princess.

sentences.zh: 煬帝又將伐遼東，謂群臣曰：「突厥狂悖為寇，勢何能為？

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was again about to attack Liaodong and said to the ministers, "The Turks are wildly rebellious as bandits—what force can they muster?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Di again prepared to attack Liaodong, he told his ministers, "The Turks are merely unruly raiders—what real threat are they?"

sentences.zh: 以其少時未散，蕭瑀遂相恐動，情不可恕。

translations.literal: Because the danger had not yet passed when he was young, Xiao Yu stirred up fear—his sentiment cannot be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis was barely over, yet Xiao Yu had spread alarm—such conduct was unforgivable."

sentences.zh: 」因出為河池郡守，即日遣之。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent out as Prefect of Hechi Commandery and dispatched the same day.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished that same day to serve as prefect of Hechi.

sentences.zh: 既至郡，有山賊萬餘人寇暴縱橫，瑀潛募勇敢之士，設奇而擊之，當陣而降其眾。

translations.literal: Once he reached the commandery, more than ten thousand mountain bandits ravaged the region unchecked; Yu secretly recruited brave men, set an ambush and struck them, and on the field of battle their host surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he found more than ten thousand mountain bandits terrorizing the region; he secretly raised brave men, ambushed them, and took their whole force in the field.

sentences.zh: 所獲財畜，咸賞有功，由是人竭其力。

translations.literal: All goods and livestock taken were rewarded to those with merit, and thereby men exhausted their strength for him.
translations.idiomatic: He gave all captured goods to those who had earned them, and men fought with all their might.

sentences.zh: 薛舉遣眾數萬侵掠郡境，瑀要擊之，自後諸賊莫敢進，郡中復安。

translations.literal: Xue Ju sent tens of thousands to raid the commandery borders; Yu intercepted and struck them, and thereafter all bandits dared not advance—the commandery was again at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju sent tens of thousands to raid the borders, Yu intercepted them; afterward no raiders dared enter and the commandery was secure again.

sentences.zh: 高祖定京城，遣書招之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu secured the capital, he sent a letter to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the capital, he sent a letter summoning Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑀以郡歸國，授光祿大夫，封宋國公，拜民部尚書。

translations.literal: Yu surrendered the commandery to the state, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Song, and made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Yu surrendered his commandery, was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Song, and appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 太宗為右元帥，攻洛陽，以瑀為府司馬。

translations.literal: When Taizong was Right Grand Marshal attacking Luoyang, Yu was made marshal of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong, as Right Grand Marshal, attacked Luoyang, Yu served as his headquarters marshal.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，遷內史令。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude he was transferred to Interior Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 5 he became interior minister.

sentences.zh: 時軍國草創，方隅未寧，高祖乃委以心腹，凡諸政務，莫不關掌。

translations.literal: At that time the army and state were newly founded and the frontiers were not yet settled; Gaozu therefore entrusted him as a confidant, and none of the various governmental affairs failed to pass through his hands.
translations.idiomatic: The state was newly founded and the borders unsettled; Gaozu made Yu his confidant, and no affair of government passed without him.

sentences.zh: 高祖每臨軒聽政，必賜升御榻，瑀既獨孤氏之婿，與語呼之為蕭郎。

translations.literal: Whenever Gaozu came to the hall to hear government, he always granted Yu ascent to the imperial couch; as Yu was son-in-law to the Dugu clan, in conversation he called him Master Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gaozu held court, he had Yu sit on the imperial couch; as the Dugu empress's son-in-law, Gaozu called him "Young Xiao" in conversation.

sentences.zh: 國典朝儀，亦責成於瑀，瑀孜孜自勉，繩違舉過，人皆憚之。

translations.literal: State statutes and court ritual were also entrusted to Yu; Yu diligently urged himself on, binding violations and citing faults, and all men feared him.
translations.idiomatic: State rites and court ceremony were also his charge; he drove himself relentlessly, citing every breach of rule, and everyone feared him.

sentences.zh: 常奏便宜數十條，多見納用，手敕曰：「得公之言，社稷所賴。

translations.literal: He often submitted several dozen timely proposals, many of which were adopted and used; a handwritten edict said, "To obtain your words is what the altars of state rely upon."
translations.idiomatic: He often submitted dozens of practical proposals, most of which Gaozu adopted; a personal edict read, "Your counsel is what the realm depends on."

sentences.zh: 運智者之策，以能成人之美；

translations.literal: To employ the strategies of the wise is to be able to complete others' excellence;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who uses wise counsel completes others' excellence;

sentences.zh: 納諫者之言，以金寶酬其德。

translations.literal: to accept the words of remonstrators and repay their virtue with gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: one who accepts remonstrance repays virtue with gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 今賜金一函，以報智者，勿為推退。

translations.literal: Now I bestow one case of gold to repay the wise man—do not decline."
translations.idiomatic: I now give you a casket of gold in thanks—do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 」瑀固辭，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Yu firmly declined, but a gracious edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu declined firmly, but a gracious edict would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 其年，州置七職，務取才望兼美者為之。

translations.literal: That year seven offices were established in each prefecture, with the aim of selecting men of combined talent and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: That year seven offices were created in each prefecture, filled only by men of talent and standing.

sentences.zh: 及太宗臨雍州牧，以瑀為州都督。

translations.literal: When Taizong assumed the post of Governor of Yong Prefecture, Yu was made regional commander of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong became governor of Yong Prefecture, Yu was made its regional commander.

sentences.zh: 高祖常有敕而中書不時宣行，高祖責其遲，瑀曰：「臣大業之日，見內史宣敕，或前後相乖者，百司行之，不知何所承用。

translations.literal: Gaozu often had edicts that the Secretariat did not promulgate in time; Gaozu blamed the delay. Yu said, "In my Daye days I saw the Secretariat promulgate edicts—sometimes those before and after contradicted each other, yet the hundred offices carried them out, not knowing which to follow."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often found edicts delayed in promulgation and blamed the Secretariat. Yu said, "In Daye times I saw edicts issued that contradicted earlier ones—yet every office obeyed, not knowing which to follow."

sentences.zh: 所謂易必在前，難必在後，臣在中書日久，備見其事。

translations.literal: What is called easy must come first and difficulty afterward; I have long been in the Secretariat and have fully witnessed these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Easy orders go out first and hard ones later—I spent years in the Secretariat and saw it all."

sentences.zh: 今皇基初構，事涉安危，遠方有疑，恐失機會。

translations.literal: Now the imperial foundation is newly built and affairs touch safety and peril; if distant regions harbor doubt, we may lose opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty is newly founded and affairs touch life and death—if distant regions grow doubtful, we may miss our chance."

sentences.zh: 比每受一敕，臣必勘審，使與前敕不相乖背者，始敢宣行。

translations.literal: Lately, whenever I receive an edict, I must examine and verify it so that it does not contradict prior edicts before I dare promulgate it.
translations.idiomatic: Now I examine every edict to ensure it does not contradict an earlier one before I dare issue it."

sentences.zh: 遲晚之愆，實由於此。

translations.literal: The fault of lateness truly stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: That is the real reason for the delay."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿能用心若此，我有何憂？

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "If you can apply your mind like this, what have I to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "If you take such care, what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」初，瑀之朝也，關內產業並先給勳人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu came to court, estates within the passes had all been given first to meritorious men.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu first came to court, estates in the Guanzhong region had already been granted to meritorious men.

sentences.zh: 至是特還其田宅，瑀皆分給諸宗子弟，唯留廟堂一所，以奉烝嘗。

translations.literal: At this time his fields and residences were specially returned; Yu distributed them all among the various clansmen and younger kin, keeping only one ancestral hall for seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Now his lands and houses were restored; he divided them among his clansmen and kept only one ancestral hall for the seasonal rites.

sentences.zh: 及平王世充，瑀以預軍謀之功，加邑二千戶，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was pacified, Yu for his merit in military planning received an additional fief of two thousand households and was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shichong was defeated, Yu's role in military planning won him two thousand added households and the post of right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 內外考績皆委之司會，為群僚指南，庶務繁總。

translations.literal: Internal and external performance reviews were all entrusted to the Director of Evaluations; he was the guide for the host of officials, and miscellaneous affairs were numerous and complex.
translations.idiomatic: All performance reviews, internal and external, went to the Director of Evaluations; he guided the bureaucracy while affairs piled up.

sentences.zh: 瑀見事有時偏駁，而持法稍深，頗為時議所少。

translations.literal: Yu saw that affairs were sometimes one-sided and partial, yet he held the law somewhat strictly and was rather slighted in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yu saw that judgments could be one-sided, yet he enforced the law sternly and drew some criticism.

sentences.zh: 瑀嘗薦封倫於高祖，高祖以倫為中書令。

translations.literal: Yu once recommended Feng Lun to Gaozu, and Gaozu made Lun Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had once recommended Feng Lun to Gaozu, who made him director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，遷尚書左僕射，封倫為右僕射。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Yu was moved to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Lun became Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded, Yu became left vice director and Lun the right vice director.

sentences.zh: 倫素懷險诐，與商量將為可奏者，至太宗前盡變易之。

translations.literal: Lun had long harbored treachery and deceit; whatever he and Yu agreed to submit, once before Taizong he changed it all.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was treacherous by nature: whatever he and Yu agreed to present, he altered entirely before Taizong.

sentences.zh: 於時房玄齡、杜如晦既新用事，疏瑀親倫，瑀心不能平，遂上封事論之，而辭旨寥落。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had newly come into power, distanced Yu and favored Lun; Yu's heart could not be at peace, and he submitted a sealed memorial discussing this, but its wording was sparse and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had just risen to power, sidelining Yu while favoring Lun; Yu, unable to accept this, submitted a sealed memorial—but its argument was thin.

sentences.zh: 太宗以玄齡等功高，由是忤旨，廢於家。

translations.literal: Taizong, because Xuanling and the others had high merit, took offense at this and dismissed Yu to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, honoring Fang and the others' merit, took offense and sent Yu home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 俄拜特進、太子少師。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Special Advancement and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Special Advancement and junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為尚書左僕射，賜實封六百戶。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted a substantive fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as left vice director and granted a substantive fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太宗常謂瑀曰：「朕欲使子孫長久，社稷永安，其理如何？

translations.literal: Taizong often said to Yu, "I wish to make my descendants endure long and the altars of state forever secure—by what principle can this be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong often asked Yu, "How can I make my line endure and the realm forever secure?"

sentences.zh: 」瑀對曰：「臣觀前代國祚所以長久者，莫若封諸侯以為盤石之固。

translations.literal: Yu replied, "I observe that in former ages what made dynastic fortunes endure was nothing so good as enfeoffing feudal lords to serve as the bedrock's solidity."
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered, "In past ages nothing secured a dynasty like enfeoffing princes as bedrock pillars of the state."

sentences.zh: 秦並六國，罷侯置守，二代而亡；

translations.literal: Qin united the six states, abolished feudal lords and set commandery governors, and perished in the second generation;
translations.idiomatic: Qin united the realm, abolished feudal lords for commandery governors, and fell in the second generation;

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，郡國參建，亦得年餘四百。

translations.literal: Han possessed the realm with commanderies and kingdoms jointly established, and also attained more than four hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruled with both commanderies and kingdoms and lasted more than four hundred years.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉廢之，不能永久。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin abolished it and could not endure long.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin abolished feudal enfeoffment and could not endure."

sentences.zh: 封建之法，實可遵行。

translations.literal: The method of feudal enfeoffment can truly be followed and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal system truly ought to be restored."

sentences.zh: 」太宗然之，始議封建。

translations.literal: Taizong approved this and began to deliberate on feudal enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong agreed and began debating the restoration of feudal princedoms.

sentences.zh: 尋坐與侍中陳叔達於上前忿諍，聲色甚厲，以不敬免。

translations.literal: Soon he was punished for quarreling angrily with Attendant-in-Ordinary Chen Shuda before the throne, his voice and expression very fierce, and was dismissed for disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he quarreled fiercely with Attendant Chen Shuda before the throne and was dismissed for disrespect.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，授晉州都督。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Regional Commander of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made regional commander of Jin.

sentences.zh: 明年，征授左光祿大夫，兼領御史大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrently made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and made censor-in-chief as well.

sentences.zh: 與宰臣參議朝政，瑀多辭辯，每有評議，玄齡等不能抗。

translations.literal: He joined the chief ministers in deliberating court government; Yu was much given to disputation, and whenever there was discussion Xuanling and the others could not withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the chief ministers in council; Yu argued tirelessly, and in debate Fang Xuanling and the others could not best him.

sentences.zh: 然心知其是，不用其言，瑀彌怏怏。

translations.literal: Yet in their hearts they knew he was right and did not use his words; Yu grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they knew he was right and ignored him—Yu grew ever more bitter.

sentences.zh: 玄齡、魏徵、溫彥博嘗有微過，瑀劾之，而罪竟不問，因此自失。

translations.literal: Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Wen Yanbo once had minor faults; Yu impeached them, yet in the end their offenses were not investigated, and because of this he lost his footing.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang, Wei Zheng, and Wen Yanbo committed minor faults, Yu impeached them—but no inquiry followed, and he lost standing.

sentences.zh: 由是罷御史大夫，以為太子少傅，不復預聞朝政。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was removed as Censor-in-Chief and made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, no longer participating in hearing court government.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed as censor-in-chief and made junior tutor to the heir apparent, no longer attending to state affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，授特進，行太常卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was granted Special Advancement and acted as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Special Advancement and acting minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，為河南道巡省大使，人有坐當推劾苦未得其情者，遂置格置繩，以至於死，太宗特免責之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made touring inspector of Henan Circuit; when persons liable to impeachment had long failed to obtain clarification of the facts, he set up a frame and rope for suspension, even to the point of death; Taizong specially exempted him from blame.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, as touring inspector of Henan Circuit, he used torture—including suspension by rope—on defendants whose cases dragged on, even causing deaths; Taizong pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜特進，復令參預政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Special Advancement and again ordered to participate in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was again made Special Advancement and restored to deliberations on government.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗從容謂房玄齡曰：「蕭瑀大業之日，進諫隋主，出為河池郡守。

translations.literal: Taizong once said calmly to Fang Xuanling, "In his Daye days Xiao Yu remonstrated with the Sui emperor and was sent out as Prefect of Hechi Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once told Fang Xuanling calmly, "In Daye times Xiao Yu remonstrated with the Sui emperor and was banished to Hechi."

sentences.zh: 應遭割心之禍，翻見太平之日，北叟失馬，事亦難常。

translations.literal: He ought to have suffered the calamity of having his heart cut out, yet instead he saw days of great peace—the old man of the north lost his horse, and affairs are also hard to make constant."
translations.idiomatic: He should have faced execution, yet lived to see peace—the old man's lost horse proves how fortune turns."

sentences.zh: 」瑀頓首拜謝。

translations.literal: Yu bowed his head to the ground in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yu kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 太宗又曰：「武德六年以後，太上皇有廢立之心而不之定也，我當此日，不為兄弟所容，實有功高不賞之懼。

translations.literal: Taizong also said, "After the sixth year of Wude the retired emperor had the intent to depose and establish but did not settle it; on that day I was not tolerated by my brothers and truly had the fear of merit too high to be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong added, "After Wude 6 the retired emperor weighed deposition but could not decide; I was not tolerated by my brothers then and truly feared that merit too great goes unrewarded."

sentences.zh: 此人不可以厚利誘之，不可以刑戮懼之，真社稷臣也。

translations.literal: This man cannot be enticed by thick profit, cannot be frightened by punishment and execution—he is truly a minister of the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: He cannot be bought with riches or cowed with punishment—he is a true pillar of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」因賜瑀詩曰：「疾風知勁草，版蕩識誠臣。

translations.literal: He thereupon bestowed on Yu a poem: "A fierce wind reveals the tough grass; turmoil reveals the loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Yu a poem: "Only in a fierce wind do you know the tough grass; only in turmoil do you know the loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 」又謂瑀曰：「卿之守道耿介，古人無以過也。

translations.literal: He also said to Yu, "Your upholding the Way is stern and unyielding—men of antiquity could not surpass it."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Yu, "Your integrity is unyielding—no man of old surpassed it."

sentences.zh: 然而善惡太明，亦有時而失。

translations.literal: Yet when good and evil are too sharply distinguished, there are also times of error."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when you draw the line between good and evil too sharply, you sometimes miss the mark."

sentences.zh: 」瑀再拜謝曰：「臣特蒙誡訓，又許臣以忠諒，雖死之日，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: Yu bowed again in thanks and said, "I have specially received your admonition and instruction, and you have also granted me loyal sincerity—even on the day of my death it will be as my years of life."
translations.idiomatic: Yu bowed again: "Your admonition honors me, and your promise of loyal candor makes even my dying day feel like life renewed."

sentences.zh: 」魏徵進而言曰：「臣有逆眾以執法，明主恕之以忠；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng stepped forward and said, "There are ministers who oppose the multitude to enforce the law, and an enlightened lord forgives them for loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng stepped forward: "Some ministers defy the crowd to enforce the law, and a wise ruler forgives them for loyalty;

sentences.zh: 臣有孤特以執節，明主恕之以勁。

translations.literal: there are ministers who stand alone to uphold integrity, and an enlightened lord forgives them for firmness."
translations.idiomatic: some stand alone to uphold integrity, and a wise ruler forgives them for their firmness."

sentences.zh: 昔聞其言，今睹其實，蕭瑀不遇明聖，必及於難！

translations.literal: I heard these words before and now behold the reality—had Xiao Yu not met a bright and sage ruler, he would surely have met with calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: I heard such words before; now I see them proved—had Xiao Yu not met a sage ruler, he would surely have come to ruin!"

sentences.zh: 」太宗悅其言。

translations.literal: Taizong was pleased with these words.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was pleased.

sentences.zh: 十七年，與長孫無忌等二十四人併圖形於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was painted together with Zhangsun Wuji and twenty-three others in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year his portrait joined those of Zhangsun Wuji and twenty-three others in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 是歲，立晉王為皇太子，拜瑀太子太保，仍知政事。

translations.literal: That year the Prince of Jin was established as Crown Prince; Yu was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and still directed government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Prince of Jin became crown prince; Yu was made grand guardian of the heir apparent while still handling government affairs.

sentences.zh: 太宗之伐遼東也，以洛邑衝要，襟帶關、河，以瑀為洛陽宮守。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, because Luoyang was strategically vital, girding the passes and the Yellow River, Yu was made keeper of the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong marched on Liaodong, he made Yu keeper of the Luoyang palace, guarding the strategic junction of the passes and the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 車駕自遼還，請解太保，仍同中書門下。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Liaodong, he requested release from the grand guardianship and still served jointly at the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return from Liaodong he asked to be relieved of the grand guardianship but continued at the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 太宗以瑀好佛道，嘗賚繡佛像一軀，並繡瑀形狀於佛像側，以為供養之容。

translations.literal: Because Taizong knew Yu favored Buddhism, he once bestowed an embroidered image of the Buddha, with Yu's likeness also embroidered beside the Buddha image, as an object for offering and worship.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yu's devotion to Buddhism, Taizong once gave him an embroidered Buddha image with Yu's own likeness worked beside it for his devotions.

sentences.zh: 又賜王褒所書《大品般若經》一部，並賜袈裟，以充講誦之服焉。

translations.literal: He also bestowed one copy of Wang Bao's transcription of the Mahaprajnaparamita Sutra and granted a kasaya robe to serve as vestments for lecturing and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave him Wang Bao's copy of the Great Prajna Sutra and a monk's robe for lecturing and recitation.

sentences.zh: 瑀嘗稱：「玄齡以下同中書門下內臣，悉皆朋黨比周，無至心奉上。

translations.literal: Yu once declared, "From Xuanling downward, all the inner ministers who serve jointly at the Central Secretariat and Chancellery are cliques banding together and have no utmost sincerity in serving the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Yu once said, "From Fang Xuanling down, every minister at the Secretariat and Chancellery is a faction-mate with no true loyalty to the throne."

sentences.zh: 」累獨奏云：「此等相與執權，有同膠漆，陛下不細諳知，但未反耳。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials alone, saying, "These men jointly hold power like glue and lacquer; Your Majesty does not know them in detail—they have simply not yet rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized alone: "They hold power together like glue—they have not rebelled only because Your Majesty does not see them clearly."

sentences.zh: 」太宗謂瑀曰：「為人君者，驅駕英材，推心待士，公言不亦甚乎，何至如此！

translations.literal: Taizong said to Yu, "As a ruler one drives and employs outstanding talent and treats scholars with open heart—is your statement not excessive? How could it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told him, "A ruler must employ talent and trust his ministers openly—is this not going too far? How can you say such things!"

sentences.zh: 」太宗數日謂瑀曰：「知臣莫若君，夫人不可求備，自當舍其短而用其長。

translations.literal: Several days later Taizong said to Yu, "No one knows a minister like his lord; one cannot demand perfection in a man—one should naturally set aside his shortcomings and use his strengths."
translations.idiomatic: Days later Taizong said, "No one knows a minister like his ruler; you cannot demand perfection—set aside faults and use strengths."

sentences.zh: 朕雖才謝聰明，不應頓迷臧否。

translations.literal: Although my talent falls short of brilliance, I ought not suddenly to be confused about right and wrong."
translations.idiomatic: I may not be the cleverest man, but I am not suddenly blind to who is right and who is wrong."

sentences.zh: 」因數為瑀信誓。

translations.literal: He therefore repeatedly gave Yu pledges and assurances.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly reassured Yu of his trust.

sentences.zh: 瑀既不自得，而太宗積久銜之，終以瑀忠貞居多而未廢也。

translations.literal: Yu was already ill at ease, and Taizong had long harbored resentment, yet in the end because Yu was mostly loyal and sincere he was not dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was discontented and Taizong had long resented him, yet in the end Yu's loyalty outweighed everything and he was not removed.

sentences.zh: 會瑀請出家，太宗謂曰：「甚知公素愛桑門，今者不能違意。

translations.literal: When Yu requested to leave the household and become a monk, Taizong said, "I well know you have always loved the Buddhist clergy; now I cannot go against your wish."
translations.idiomatic: When Yu asked to take Buddhist orders, Taizong said, "I know you have always loved the monastic life—I will not stand in your way."

sentences.zh: 」瑀旋踵奏曰：「臣頃思量，不能出家。

translations.literal: Yu immediately turned and memorialized, "I have just reflected and cannot leave the household."
translations.idiomatic: Yu immediately turned back: "On reflection, I cannot leave the household after all."

sentences.zh: 」太宗以對群臣吐言，而取捨相違，心不能平。

translations.literal: Taizong, because he had spoken this before the assembled ministers yet Yu's choice and rejection conflicted, could not be at peace in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had spoken before the whole court, yet Yu reversed himself—he could not be reconciled.

sentences.zh: 瑀尋稱足疾，時詣朝堂，又不入見，太宗謂侍臣曰：「瑀豈不得其所乎，而自慊如此？

translations.literal: Yu soon claimed foot ailment; sometimes he came to the court hall yet did not enter for audience. Taizong said to the attending ministers, "Has Yu not found his place, that he is so discontented on his own?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu soon claimed a foot ailment; he would come to court yet refuse audience. Taizong told his attendants, "Has Yu not found his place, that he sulks like this?"

sentences.zh: 」遂手詔曰：

translations.literal: He thereupon wrote a personal edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then drafted a personal edict:

sentences.zh: 朕聞物之順也，雖異質而成功；

translations.literal: I have heard that when things accord, though their substance differs they succeed;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when things work in harmony, different natures may still succeed together;

sentences.zh: 事之違也，亦同形而罕用。

translations.literal: When affairs go against [harmony], though the form is the same they are seldom effective.
translations.idiomatic: But when matters run counter to harmony, likeness of form rarely avails.

sentences.zh: 是以舟浮楫舉，可濟千里之川；

translations.literal: Thus when a boat floats and oars are raised, one may cross rivers a thousand li long;
translations.idiomatic: A boat that floats and oars that pull can carry you a thousand li along the rivers;

sentences.zh: 轅引輪停，不越一毫之地。

translations.literal: when the yoke pulls and the wheels stop, one cannot pass even a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: yet if the yoke strains and the wheels do not turn, not even a hair's breadth of ground is gained.

sentences.zh: 故知動靜相循易為務，曲直相反難為功，況乎上下之宜、君臣之際者矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that when movement and stillness follow each other the task is easy, but when crooked and straight oppose each other achievement is hard—how much more so for the fitness of superior and subordinate and the junction of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that when motion and rest take turns, the work goes easily, but when what bends and what stands straight pull against each other, success is hard—above all in the propriety between ruler and ruled and in the bond between sovereign and minister.

sentences.zh: 朕以無明於元首，期托德於股肱，思欲去偽歸真，除澆反朴。

translations.literal: I, lacking clarity as the head [of state], look to rely on virtue in my arms and legs, and think to cast off falsity and return to truth, remove the watered-down and restore the plain.
translations.idiomatic: I lack clear judgment at the helm of the state and look to my ministers for steadfast virtue; I mean to strip away pretense for what is true and wash away decadence for plainness again.

sentences.zh: 至於佛教，非意所遵，雖有國之常經，固弊俗之虛術。

translations.literal: As for Buddhism, it is not what my heart follows; though it has become the routine scripture of the realm, it is after all the empty art of a corrupt custom.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is not the path my heart follows; though it has become established national practice, it remains at bottom a hollow fashion of a decadent age.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 求其道者，未驗福於將來；

translations.literal: Those who seek its Way have not verified blessings in what is to come;
translations.idiomatic: Those who pursue its teachings have never proved future blessing;

sentences.zh: 修其教者，翻受辜於既往。

translations.literal: those who cultivate its teaching on the contrary have borne guilt in what is past.
translations.idiomatic: those who keep its rites have instead suffered for what is already past.

sentences.zh: 至若梁武窮心於釋氏，簡文銳意於法門，傾帑藏以給僧祗，殫人力以供塔廟。

translations.literal: As for Liang Wudi exhausting his heart on the Shakya clan, Emperor Jianwen sharpening his purpose on the Dharma gate, emptying the treasury stores to supply the sangha, and exhausting human strength to supply pagodas and temples—
translations.idiomatic: Consider Liang Wudi, who gave his whole heart to the Buddha's teaching, and Emperor Jianwen, who threw himself into the Dharma—emptying the treasury for monks and draining the people to build towers and temples.

sentences.zh: 及乎三淮沸浪，五嶺騰煙，假餘息於熊蹯，引殘魂於雀谷。

translations.literal: When the three Huai boiled in waves and the five Linges rose in smoke, they borrowed a last breath at Bear's Foot and drew their lingering souls to Sparrow Valley.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai regions churned and the Lingnan hills smoked, they clung to a last breath at Xionger Mountain and dragged their dying souls to Que'gu.

sentences.zh: 子孫覆亡而不暇，社稷俄頃而為墟，報施之征，何其繆也！

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons perished with no time to spare; altars of state in an instant became ruins—how perverse were the signs of retributive recompense!
translations.idiomatic: Their heirs were wiped out before they could look back; their altars of state became rubble in a moment—what a perverse proof of reward and punishment!

sentences.zh: 而太子太保、宋國公瑀踐覆車之餘軌，襲亡國之遺風。

translations.literal: Yet Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Song Yu tread the ruts left by the overturned cart and follow the lingering winds of a perished state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Grand Guardian and Duke of Song, Yu, walks again in tracks where carts overturned and takes up the surviving manners of fallen kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 棄公就私，未明隱顯之際；

translations.literal: He abandons the public for the private and does not discern the juncture between hidden and manifest;
translations.idiomatic: He forsakes his public duty for private ends and cannot tell when to conceal and when to show himself;

sentences.zh: 身俗口道，莫辯邪正之心。

translations.literal: in body worldly and in mouth preaching the Way, he cannot distinguish the mind of the heterodox from the orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: worldly in his person and doctrinaire on his tongue, he no longer knows what is crooked and what is straight in his own heart.

sentences.zh: 修累葉之殃源，祈一躬之福本，上以違忤君主，下則扇習浮華。

translations.literal: He cultivates the sources of calamity accumulated through many generations and prays for the root of blessing in one person alone; above he defies the lord; below he fans and spreads flashy fashions.
translations.idiomatic: He nurtures disasters piled up through generations yet prays for blessings for himself alone—above, he offends his sovereign; below, he spreads vain display among the people.

sentences.zh: 往前朕謂張亮云：「卿既事佛，何不出家？

translations.literal: Earlier I said to Zhang Liang: "Since you serve the Buddha, why do you not leave home and become a monk?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier I said to Zhang Liang, "You serve the Buddha—why not take the tonsure and leave the world?

sentences.zh: 」瑀乃端然自應，請先入道，朕即許之，尋復不用。

translations.literal: " Yu then solemnly responded on his own behalf, asking first to enter the Way; I at once granted it, but soon did not employ [the grant].
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered with composed dignity that he wished to enter the religious life first; I agreed at once, then soon withdrew that approval.

sentences.zh: 一回一惑，在於瞬息之間；

translations.literal: One turning and one confusion lie within the space of a blink;
translations.idiomatic: One moment yes, the next in doubt—all within the blink of an eye;

sentences.zh: 自可自否，變於帷扆之所。

translations.literal: at his own pleasure affirming and denying, he changes within the place of curtains and throne.
translations.idiomatic: affirming and denying as he pleased, shifting his stance even before the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 乖棟樑之大體，豈具瞻之量乎？

translations.literal: He violates the great substance of pillar and beam—how could he possess the measure of one on whom all eyes depend?
translations.idiomatic: He betrays the bearing owed a pillar of the realm—how can he possess the stature on which all eyes depend?

sentences.zh: 朕猶隱忍至今，瑀尚全無悛改。

translations.literal: I have still borne with him in forbearance until now, yet Yu still shows no repentance or change.
translations.idiomatic: I have restrained myself until today, yet Yu has shown no repentance at all.

sentences.zh: 宜即去茲朝闕，出牧小籓，可商州刺史，仍除其封。

translations.literal: He should at once leave these court gates, go out to shepherd a small frontier—he may be made Governor of Shangzhou, and his fief is also to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Let him leave the capital at once and govern a lesser commandery; appoint him Governor of Shangzhou and strip his noble title.

sentences.zh: 子銳嗣，尚太宗女襄城公主，歷太常卿、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Rui succeeded; he married Emperor Taizong's daughter Princess Xiangcheng and served successively as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Governor of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui inherited the line, married Princess Xiangcheng, a daughter of Taizong, and rose through the posts of Minister of Rites and Governor of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 公主雅有禮度，太宗每令諸公主，凡厥所為，皆視其楷則。

translations.literal: The princess had elegant ritual propriety; Taizong often told the various princesses that whatever they did should take her as the standard pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was a model of decorum; Taizong often told the other imperial daughters to take whatever she did as their standard.

sentences.zh: 又令所司別為營第，公主辭曰：「婦人事舅姑如事父母，若居處不同，則定省多闕。

translations.literal: He also ordered the relevant offices to build a separate residence; the princess declined, saying: "A wife serves her husband's parents as she serves her own parents; if our dwellings differ, morning and evening visits will often be wanting."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered officials to build her a separate mansion, but the princess declined: "A wife tends her husband's parents as her own; if we lived apart, I could not attend them morning and evening."

sentences.zh: 」再三固讓，乃止，令於舊宅而改創焉。

translations.literal: After repeatedly firm refusals it stopped; he ordered renovation and rebuilding at the old residence.
translations.idiomatic: After she firmly refused again and again, he relented and had the old house renovated instead.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，公主薨，詔葬昭陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, the princess died; an edict ordered burial at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui era the princess died, and the court ordered her buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 瑀兄璟，亦有學行。

translations.literal: Yu's elder brother Jing likewise had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's older brother Jing was likewise learned and upright in conduct.

sentences.zh: 武德中為黃門侍郎，累轉秘書監，封蘭陵縣公。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he was Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; he was promoted in stages to Director of the Imperial Library and enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling county.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, was promoted to Director of the Imperial Library, and was enfeoffed Duke of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the Zhenguan era; posthumously he was given Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Zhenguan period and was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 瑀兄子鈞，隋遷州刺史、梁國公珣之子也。

translations.literal: Yu's elder brother's son Jun was the son of Sui's Governor of Qianzhou and Duke of Liang state Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's nephew Jun was the son of Xun, who had been Sui Governor of Qianzhou and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 博學有才望。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, with talent and renown.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply learned and widely esteemed.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累除中書舍人，甚為房玄齡、魏徵所重。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he was promoted in stages to Zhongshu Sheren; Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he rose through appointments to Palace Draftsman and won high regard from Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，歷遷諫議大夫，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he was promoted in stages to Remonstrating and Proposing Grand Master, concurrently Academician of the Hongwen Guan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui he was promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master and made a concurrent scholar of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 時有左武候別駕盧文操，逾垣盜左藏庫物，高宗以別駕職在糾繩，身行盜竊，命有司殺之。

translations.literal: At the time there was Left Martial Guard Assistant Commissioner Lu Wencao, who scaled the wall and stole goods from the Left Treasury; Gaozong, on the grounds that the assistant commissioner's office was to restrain and bind wrongdoing, yet he personally committed theft, ordered the authorities to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Left Martial Guard assistant commissioner Lu Wencao climbed a wall and stole from the Left Treasury; Gaozong reasoned that a man whose duty was to punish crime had himself stolen, and ordered him put to death.

sentences.zh: 鈞進諫曰：「文操所犯，情實難原。

translations.literal: Jun advanced a remonstrance, saying: "Wencao's offense—its circumstances are truly hard to excuse."
translations.idiomatic: Jun remonstrated: "What Wencao did is indeed hard to forgive.

sentences.zh: 然恐天下聞之，必謂陛下輕法律，賤人命，任喜怒，貴財物。

translations.literal: Yet I fear that when the realm hears of it, they will surely say that Your Majesty treats the law lightly, esteems human life cheaply, indulges anger and pleasure, and prizes goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that when the realm hears of this they will say Your Majesty holds law cheap, life cheaper still, and lets mood and treasure outweigh justice.

sentences.zh: 臣之所職，以諫為名，愚衷所懷，不敢不奏。

translations.literal: My office is named for remonstrance; what my foolish heart harbors I dare not fail to present.
translations.idiomatic: My office is called remonstrance; what my foolish heart feels I dare not withhold.

sentences.zh: 」帝謂曰：「卿職在司諫，能盡忠規。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "Your office lies in supervising remonstrance; you can exhaust loyal admonition."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your charge is remonstrance, and you have fulfilled it with loyal candor.

sentences.zh: 」遂特免其死罪，顧謂侍臣曰：「此乃真諫議也。

translations.literal: He thereupon specially exempted him from the death penalty, turned to the attendant ministers and said: "This is a true remonstrating and proposing [grand master]."
translations.idiomatic: He then specially spared Wencao's life and told the attending ministers, "This is what a true remonstrator looks like.

sentences.zh: 」尋而太常樂工宋四通等，為宮人通傳信物，高宗特令處死，乃遣附律，鈞上疏言：「四通等犯在未附律前，不合至死。

translations.literal: Soon after, Director of Court Music workers Song Sitong and others had conveyed messages and goods for palace women; Gaozong specially ordered execution; later the law was appended and Jun submitted a memorial saying: "Sitong and the others offended before the law was appended—they should not have been punished with death."
translations.idiomatic: Soon court musicians Song Sitong and others were caught passing messages for palace women; Gaozong ordered them executed, then had the statute amended retroactively; Jun memorialized that their crime predated the law and death was not warranted.

sentences.zh: 」手詔曰：「朕聞防禍未萌，先賢所重，宮闕之禁，其可漸歟？

translations.literal: Personal edict: "I have heard that preventing calamity before it sprouts is what the ancient worthies prized; the prohibitions of palace and forbidden quarter—can these grow lax bit by bit?"
translations.idiomatic: A personal edict answered: "I know the ancients prized stopping trouble before it sprouted—can palace discipline be allowed to slip by degrees?

sentences.zh: 昔如姬竊符，朕用為永鑑，不欲今茲自彰其過，所搦憲章，想非濫也。

translations.literal: In former times Ru Ji stole the tally—I take that as an everlasting mirror; I do not wish that today's faults should make themselves conspicuous; the legal code grasped—I trust it is not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Lady Ru stole the tally and brought down a state—I keep that before me always. I do not mean these men to expose their own guilt in public, and I trust the law I apply is not excessive.

sentences.zh: 但朕翹心紫禁，思覿引裾，側席硃楹，冀旌折檻。

translations.literal: Yet I eagerly lift my heart to the Forbidden Purple; I think of seeing [such as] pulling the robe's hem; I sit sidelong by red pillars, hoping to mark the broken balustrade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I lean toward the palace not to silence counsel but to hear it—I keep my seat askew at the red pillars, hoping for men who would break the balustrade to speak.

sentences.zh: 今乃喜得其言，特免四通等死，遠處配流。

translations.literal: Now I am pleased to obtain such words; I specially spare Sitong and others from death and send them far away to penal exile.
