translations.idiomatic: Now I am glad of your words and specially spare Sitong and the rest from death, sending them instead to distant exile.

sentences.zh: 」鈞尋為太子率更令，兼崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: Jun was soon made Crown Prince's Director of Palace Stud and concurrent Academician of the Chongxian Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was soon made Director of Palace Stud for the heir apparent and concurrent scholar of the Chongxian Academy.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Xianqing era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xianqing era.

sentences.zh: 所撰《韻旨》二十捲，有集三十捲行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled "Rhyme Essentials" in twenty juan; he had a collected works of thirty juan that circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Rhyme Essentials in twenty scrolls and left collected works in thirty scrolls that circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子瓘，官至渝州長史。

translations.literal: His son Guan rose to office as Senior Administrator of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan rose as senior administrator of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 母終，以毀卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he died from the severity of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he died from grief's severity.

sentences.zh: 瓘子嵩，別有傳。

translations.literal: Guan's son Song has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's son Song is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 鈞兄子嗣業，少隨祖姑隋煬帝后入於突厥。

translations.literal: Jun's elder brother's son Sizye in youth followed his father's elder sister, Sui Emperor Yang's empress, into the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's nephew Sizye went in his youth with the former Sui empress—his grand-aunt—into the Turks.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年歸朝，以深識蕃情充使，統領突厥之眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan he returned to the court; because of his deep knowledge of barbarian affairs he was made envoy and led the Turkic hosts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan he returned; his keen knowledge of frontier peoples made him envoy commanding Turk forces.

sentences.zh: 累轉鴻臚卿，兼單于都護府長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception and concurrently Senior Administrator of the Chanyu Protectorate Office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through promotions to Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception and concurrent chief administrator of the Chanyu Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 調露中，單于突厥反叛，嗣業率兵戰，敗，配流嶺南而死。

translations.literal: In the Tiaolu era the Chanyu Turks rebelled; Sizye led troops to battle, was defeated, and was sentenced to penal exile in Lingnan, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiaolu the Turks of the protectorate rebelled; Sizye led troops against them, was defeated, and died in exile in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 裴矩，字弘大，河東聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Ju, style name Hongda, a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju, styled Hongda, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖佗，後魏東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tuo was Eastern Jingzhou Inspector of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tuo was Eastern Jingzhou inspector under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父訥之，北齊太子舍人。

translations.literal: His father Nezhi was Crown Prince Attendant of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nezhi served as attendant to the crown prince of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 矩襁褓而孤，為伯父讓之所鞠。

translations.literal: Ju was orphaned in swaddling clothes and was reared by his father's elder brother Rangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ju lost his father in infancy and was raised by his uncle Rangzhi.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學，早知名，仕齊為高平王文學。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly learned, early renowned, and served Qi as literary aide to the Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was widely learned and known early; in Qi he served as literary tutor to the Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，隋文帝為定州總管，召補記室，甚親敬之。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, Emperor Wen of Sui as Governor-General of Dingzhou summoned him to fill the post of Secretariat Recorder and treated him with great intimacy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, while still governor-general of Dingzhou the future Emperor Wen summoned him as secretariat recorder and treated him with warm regard.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，遷給事郎，直內史省，奏舍人事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman, served directly in the Secretariat Office, and performed matters as Secretariat Receiving Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen took the throne he was made an attendant gentleman, served in the Secretariat, and handled memorials as receiving clerk.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，領元帥記室。

translations.literal: In the campaign to conquer Chen he headed the commander-in-chief's Secretariat Recorder staff.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen he served as chief secretariat officer to the commander.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，晉王廣令矩與高颎收陳圖籍，歸之秘府。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, Prince of Jin Guang ordered Ju and Gao Jiong to collect Chen's maps and registers and return them to the secret archives.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell, Prince Guang sent Ju with Gao Jiong to gather Chen's archives for the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部侍郎，以事免。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Vice Minister of the Civil Service and was dismissed over an affair.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of civil appointments but was dismissed over a matter.

sentences.zh: 大業初，西域諸蕃款張掖塞與中國互市，煬帝遣矩監其事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, the various western barbarians presented themselves sincerely at the Zhangye passes to trade with China; Emperor Yang sent Ju to supervise the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye, western peoples came in goodwill to Zhangye to trade with China, and Yangdi sent Ju to oversee the markets.

sentences.zh: 矩知帝方勤遠略，欲吞併夷狄，乃訪西域風俗及山川險易、君長姓族、物產服章，撰《西域圖記》三卷，入朝奏之。

translations.literal: Ju knew the emperor was then laboring at distant strategy and wished to swallow up the Yi and Di; he therefore inquired into western regions' customs and the ease or difficulty of mountains and rivers, chieftains' surnames and clans, products, and dress insignia, compiled "Illustrated Record of the Western Regions" in three juan, and entering court presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor bent on distant conquest and bent on absorbing the frontier peoples, Ju investigated western customs, terrain, rulers and clans, products, and dress, compiled an Illustrated Record of the Western Regions in three scrolls, and presented it at court.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him with five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 每日引至御座，顧問西方之事。

translations.literal: Each day he was led to the imperial seat and consulted on matters of the west.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he was summoned to the throne to answer questions on the west.

sentences.zh: 矩盛言西域多珍寶及吐谷渾可並之狀，帝信之。

translations.literal: Ju exuberantly spoke of how the western lands had many treasures and how Tuyuhun could be annexed; the emperor believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ju spoke at length of western treasures and of how Tuyuhun might be annexed, and the emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 仍委以經略，拜民部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again entrusted with strategic planning and appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Yangdi entrusted him with frontier strategy and made him vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 俄遷黃門侍郎，參預朝政。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and participated in deliberating government.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and admitted to policy deliberations.

sentences.zh: 令往張掖引致西蕃，至者十餘國。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Zhangye to draw in the western barbarians; more than ten states arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Zhangye to attract western peoples, and more than a dozen states came.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝有事於恆岳，咸來助祭。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor had business at Mount Heng; all came to assist in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the emperor sacrificed at Mount Heng, they all came to join the rites.

sentences.zh: 帝將巡河右，復令矩往燉煌，矩遣使說高昌王鞠伯雅及伊吾吐屯設等，啖以厚利，導使入朝。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to tour the west of the Yellow River and again ordered Ju to Dunhuang; Ju sent envoys to persuade King Qu Boya of Gaochang and the Tutan she of Yiwu and others, baiting them with thick profits and guiding them to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a tour of the Hexi corridor he again sent Ju to Dunhuang; Ju's envoys persuaded King Qu Boya of Gaochang and the Yiwu chieftain with rich inducements to come to court.

sentences.zh: 及帝西巡，次燕支山，高昌王、伊吾設等及西蕃胡二十七國，盛服珠玉錦罽，焚香奏樂，歌舞相趨，謁於道左。

translations.literal: When the emperor made his western tour and halted at Yanzhi Mountain, the King of Gaochang, the Yiwu she, and twenty-seven western Hu states, in splendid dress of pearls, jade, brocades and felts, burned incense and played music, dancing toward one another, paid court on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: On the western tour the emperor stopped at Yanzhi Mountain; the King of Gaochang, the Yiwu chieftain, and twenty-seven western states came in splendid dress of pearl, jade, and brocade, with incense and music, dancing forward to pay homage along the road.

sentences.zh: 復令武威、張掖士女盛飾縱觀，填咽周亙數十里，帝見之大悅。

translations.literal: He again ordered men and women of Wuwei and Zhangye to dress splendidly and gaze broadly; they packed and choked the circuit for several tens of li; the emperor saw it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He had the men and women of Wuwei and Zhangye turn out in their finest to watch; for tens of li the roads were packed, and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 及滅吐谷渾，蠻夷納貢，諸蕃懾服，相繼來庭。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun was destroyed, the barbarians presented tribute; the various fan were overawed and submitted in succession, coming to court one after another.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuyuhun was destroyed, frontier peoples sent tribute; one after another they came to court in submission.

sentences.zh: 雖拓地數千里，而役戍委輸之費，歲巨萬計，中國騷動焉。

translations.literal: Though territory was extended several thousand li, the costs of corvée labor, garrison service, and transport of supplies amounted annually to tens of thousands; China was stirred and troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Though the empire stretched thousands of li further, corvée, garrison, and transport costs ran to tens of thousands yearly and the heartland was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 帝以矩有綏懷之略，加位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Ju had a strategy of soothing and cherishing, added the rank of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Honors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor credited Ju with a policy of winning hearts on the frontier and promoted him to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Honors.

sentences.zh: 其年，帝至東都，矩以蠻夷朝貢者多，諷帝大征四方奇技，作魚龍曼延角牴於洛邑，以誇諸戎狄，終月而罷。

translations.literal: That year the emperor reached the Eastern Capital; Ju, because many barbarians came in tribute, subtly urged the emperor to muster exotic skills from the four quarters and stage fish-dragon, many-extending, and wrestling performances at Luoyang to show off to the various Rong and Di; after a full month it ended.
translations.idiomatic: That year, at the Eastern Capital, with many tributaries present Ju urged the emperor to summon exotic entertainments from the four quarters—aquatic pageants, acrobatics, and wrestling in Luoyang to dazzle the frontier envoys, and the displays ran a full month.

sentences.zh: 又令三市店肆皆設帷帳，盛酒食，遣掌蕃率蠻夷與人貿易，所至處悉令邀延就座，醉飽而散。

translations.literal: He also ordered the three markets' shops all to set up curtains and tents, with abundant wine and food, and sent those in charge of barbarians to lead the barbarians to trade with the people; wherever they arrived all were ordered to invite and detain them to take seats, and they scattered drunken and full.
translations.idiomatic: He also draped the market stalls, set out feasts, and had frontier commissioners host the envoys in trade and hospitality—wherever they went they were pressed to sit, eat, and drink their fill before dispersing.

sentences.zh: 夷人有識者，咸私哂其矯飾焉。

translations.literal: Among the Yi those with understanding all privately ridiculed this artifice and ornamentation.
translations.idiomatic: The more discerning among the envoys privately mocked the show.

sentences.zh: 帝稱矩至誠，謂宇文述、牛弘曰：「裴矩大識朕意，凡所陳奏，皆朕之成算，朕未發頃，矩輒以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Ju's utmost sincerity and said to Yuwen Shu and Niu Hong: "Pei Ju greatly knows my mind; whatever he presents in memorial—all are my completed plans; before I have sent out a thought, Ju has already reported it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Ju's devotion and told Yuwen Shu and Niu Hong, "Pei Ju understands my mind. Whatever he memorializes is already my settled plan—before I have spoken, Ju has already reported it.

sentences.zh: 自非奉國用心，孰能若是？

translations.literal: Unless one serves the state with one's heart, who could be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Who but a man devoted to the realm could do such a thing?

sentences.zh: 」尋令與將軍薛世雄城伊吾而還，賜錢四十萬。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered with General Xue Shixiong to fortify Yiwu and return; forty thousand cash were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent with General Xue Shixiong to build fortifications at Yiwu and return, and was rewarded with four hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 矩因進計縱反間於射匱，使潛攻處羅。

translations.literal: Ju thereupon advanced a plan to set loose a counter-alliance plot toward Shekui, causing him to attack Chuluo in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Ju then proposed a ruse to sow discord with Shekui and induce him to strike Qaghan Chuluo.

sentences.zh: 後處羅為射匱所迫，竟隨使者入朝，帝甚悅，賜矩貂裘及西域珍器。

translations.literal: Later Chuluo was pressed by Shekui and in the end followed envoys to enter court; the emperor was very pleased and bestowed on Ju a sable fur coat and western-region rare vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chuluo, pressed by Shekui, came to court with the envoys; the emperor was pleased and gave Ju a sable cloak and rare objects from the west.

sentences.zh: 從帝巡於塞北，幸啟民可汗帳。

translations.literal: Following the emperor he toured north of the passes and visited Qimin Qaghan's tent.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on a tour north of the frontier and visited Qimin Qaghan's camp.

sentences.zh: 時高麗遣使先通於突厥，啟民不敢隱，引之見帝。

translations.literal: At the time Goguryeo had sent envoys to communicate first with the Turks; Qimin dared not conceal it and led them to see the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Goguryeo had sent envoys to the Turks first; Qimin did not conceal it and presented them to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 矩因奏曰：「高麗之地，本孤竹國也，周代以之封箕子，漢時分為三郡，晉氏亦統遼東。

translations.literal: Ju thereupon memorialized, saying: "The land of Goguryeo was originally the state of Guzhu; in Zhou it was enfeoffed to Jizi; in Han it was divided into three commanderies; Jin also ruled Liaodong."
translations.idiomatic: Ju memorialized: "Goguryeo's territory was once the state of Guzhu; Zhou enfeoffed Jizi there; Han divided it into three commanderies; Jin too held Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 今乃不臣，列為外域，故先帝欲征之久矣，但以楊諒不肖，師出無功。

translations.literal: Now it will not submit and is ranked as outer territory; therefore the former emperor long wished to campaign against it, but because Yang Liang was unworthy the army went out without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Now it refuses allegiance and stands outside the empire; the former emperor long meant to chastise it, but Yang Liang's rebellion left campaigns unfinished.

sentences.zh: 當陛下時，安得不有事於此，使冠帶之境，仍為蠻貊之鄉乎？

translations.literal: In Your Majesty's time, how can there fail to be business with this—so that the realm of cap and sash still remains a land of barbarians and Mo?
translations.idiomatic: Under Your Majesty, how can we leave it so that lands once within cap-and-gown still remain barbarian country?

sentences.zh: 今其使者朝於突厥，親見啟民從化，必懼皇靈之遠暢，慮後服之先亡，脅令入朝，當可致也。

translations.literal: Now its envoys pay court to the Turks and personally see Qimin's following-the-transformation; they will surely fear the far-reaching brightness of the imperial numen and worry that late submission will perish first; if we coerce them to enter court, it can be brought about.
translations.idiomatic: Now its envoys have seen Qimin submit at the Turk court; they will fear the reach of imperial power and worry that those who come last will perish first—if we press them to court, they may be brought in.

sentences.zh: 請面詔其使還本國，遣詔其王令速朝覲。

translations.literal: I request that you face-to-face instruct their envoy to return to his state and send an edict to their king ordering swift attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: Summon their envoy and order him home with an edict that the king come at once to court.

sentences.zh: 不然者，當率突厥即日誅之。

translations.literal: If not, we should lead the Turks that very day to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise lead the Turks against them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 」帝納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 高麗不用命，始建征遼之策。

translations.literal: Goguryeo did not obey orders; the plan to campaign against Liaodong was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo disobeyed, and the plan for the Liaodong campaign was set in motion.

sentences.zh: 王師臨遼，以本官領虎賁郎將。

translations.literal: When the royal army reached Liaodong he in his original office headed the Tiger-Gallant Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army reached Liaodong he served in his existing rank as commander of the Tiger-Gallant guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，復從至遼東。

translations.literal: The next year, again following, they reached Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again accompanied the emperor to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎斛斯政亡入高麗，帝令矩兼掌兵部事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Husizheng fled into Goguryeo; the emperor ordered Ju concurrently to manage Ministry of War affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Husizheng had fled to Goguryeo, and the emperor put Ju in charge of War Ministry affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 以前後渡遼功，進位右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because of achievements before and after crossing Liaodong, he was advanced to Right Grand Master of Palace Honors.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the Liaodong crossings he was promoted to Right Grand Master of Palace Honors.

sentences.zh: 矩後從幸江都。

translations.literal: Ju later followed on the journey of fortune to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Ju later accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 及義兵入關，屈突通敗問至，帝問矩方略，矩曰：「太原有變，京畿不靜，遙為處分，恐失事機。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered the passes, news of Qu Tuotong's defeat arrived; the emperor asked Ju for strategy, and Ju said: "Taiyuan has changed; the capital region is not calm; to dispose of affairs from afar, I fear we will miss the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel forces entered the passes and word came of Qu Tuotong's defeat, the emperor asked Ju's counsel. Ju said, "Taiyuan has risen and the heartland is unsettled; to govern from here at a distance is to miss the moment.

sentences.zh: 唯鑾輿早還，方可平定。

translations.literal: Only if the imperial carriage returns early can order be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty returns to the north soon can the realm be pacified."

sentences.zh: 」矩見天下將亂，恐為身禍，每遇人盡禮，雖至胥吏，皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: Ju saw the realm about to fall into chaos and feared harm to himself; whenever he met people he showed full courtesy, even down to clerks, and all obtained his good will.
translations.idiomatic: Ju saw the empire slipping toward chaos and feared for his own safety; he treated everyone with full courtesy, even low clerks, and won their goodwill.

sentences.zh: 時從駕驍果多逃散，矩言於帝曰：「車駕留此，已經二歲，人無匹合，則不能久安。

translations.literal: At the time many of the escort's brave fruit guards had fled and scattered; Ju spoke to the emperor, saying: "The carriage has stayed here already two years; men without mates cannot long stay settled.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the emperor's elite guards had deserted; Ju told him, "You have been at Jiangdu two years. Men without wives cannot remain content for long.

sentences.zh: 請聽兵士於此納室，私相奔誘者，因而配之。

translations.literal: I request that soldiers be allowed to take wives here; those who privately lure one another, let them be paired accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Allow the soldiers to marry here—match those who have courted on their own."

sentences.zh: 」帝從其計，軍中漸安，咸曰：「裴公之惠也。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his plan; the army gradually settled, all saying: "It is Lord Pei's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; the army grew steadier, and men said, "It was Lord Pei's doing."

sentences.zh: 」是時，帝既昏侈逾甚，矩無所諫諍，但悅媚取容而已。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was already ever more muddled and extravagant; Ju had no remonstrance, but only pleased and flattered to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor was sunk in luxury; Ju offered no remonstrance and only pleased him to remain in favor.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弒逆，署為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji committed regicide; Ju was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, he made Ju Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，竇建德復以為尚書右僕射，令專掌選事。

translations.literal: After Huaji was defeated, Dou Jiande again made him Right Vice Director and ordered him to specialize in appointment affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji's fall Dou Jiande made him Right Vice Director again and put him in charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 時建德起自群盜，事無節文，矩為之創定朝儀，權設法律，憲章頗備，建德大悅，每諮訪焉。

translations.literal: At the time Jiande had risen from bandits and affairs lacked ritual forms; Ju for him created and fixed court ceremony, provisionally set laws, and statutes were quite complete; Jiande was greatly pleased and often consulted him thereon.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande had risen from banditry and had no court ritual; Ju devised ceremony and provisional laws until the regime had a full code. Jiande was delighted and constantly sought his advice.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，矩與偽將曹旦及建德之妻齎傳國八璽，舉山東之地來降，封安邑縣公。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, Ju with the false general Cao Dan and Jiande's wife carried the eight imperial seals of succession and raised the Shandong lands to submit; he was enfeoffed Duke of Anyi county.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande's defeat Ju came over with the rebel general Cao Dan and Jiande's wife, bringing the eight dynastic seals and offering Shandong; he was created Duke of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，拜太子左庶子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude he was appointed Left Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year five he became Left Companion to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 俄遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 令與虞世南撰《吉凶書儀》，參按故實，甚合禮度，為學者所稱，至今行之。

translations.literal: He was ordered with Yu Shinan to compile Auspicious and Inauspicious Letter Rites, checking against ancient practice; it greatly accorded with ritual measure, was praised by scholars, and is practiced to this day.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yu Shinan were commissioned to compile Rites of Auspicious and Inauspicious Correspondence, drawn from precedent and fully consonant with ritual; scholars praised it and it remains in use.

sentences.zh: 八年，兼檢校侍中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he concurrently served as supervising Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he also served as Acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及太子建成被誅，其餘黨尚保宮城，欲與秦王決戰，王遣矩曉諭之，宮兵乃散。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent Jiancheng was executed, the remnant faction still held the palace city and wished to join in decisive battle with the Prince of Qin; the prince sent Ju to enlighten and persuade them, and the palace troops then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Jiancheng was killed his partisans still held the palace and meant to fight the Prince of Qin; the prince sent Ju to reason with them and the garrison dispersed.

sentences.zh: 尋遷民部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 矩年且八十，而精爽不衰，以曉習故事，甚見推重。

translations.literal: Ju was nearly eighty years old yet his spirit was undiminished; because he was versed in precedent he was greatly esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly eighty, he remained keen-minded; his mastery of precedent won deep respect.

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，務止奸吏，或聞諸曹案典，多有受賂者，乃遣人以財物試之。

translations.literal: When Taizong first took the throne he strove to stop corrupt clerks; he heard that in the various bureaus many case handlers took bribes, and so sent men to test them with goods.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taizong's reign he moved against corrupt officials; hearing that many clerks took bribes, he sent men to tempt them with goods.

sentences.zh: 有司門令史受饋絹一匹，太宗怒，將殺之，矩進諫曰：「此人受賂，誠合重誅。

translations.literal: A gate-department clerk accepted a bribe of one bolt of silk; Taizong was angry and was about to execute him; Ju advanced a remonstrance, saying: "This man accepted a bribe and indeed deserves heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A gate clerk accepted one bolt of silk as a bribe; Taizong was furious and would have executed him. Ju remonstrated: "Taking a bribe deserves severe punishment,

sentences.zh: 但陛下以物試之，即行極法，所謂陷人以罪，恐非導德齊禮之義。

translations.literal: But Your Majesty tested him with goods and immediately applied the extreme penalty—this is what is called entrapping a man into crime; I fear it is not the meaning of guiding virtue and aligning ritual.
translations.idiomatic: but to tempt him and then apply the death penalty is to entrap a man in guilt and hardly accords with guiding the realm by virtue and ritual."

sentences.zh: 」太宗納其言，因召百僚謂曰：「裴矩遂能廷折，不肯面從，每事如此，天下何憂不治！

translations.literal: Taizong adopted his words and thereupon summoned the hundred officials, saying: "Pei Ju can dispute at court and refuse to follow to the face; if every matter is thus, what worry is there that the realm will not be governed!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accepted his counsel and told the assembled officials, "Pei Ju can argue me down in open court and will not simply agree to my face. If every minister did so, what fear would we have for good government!"

sentences.zh: 」貞觀元年卒，贈絳州刺史，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he died; posthumously he was made prefect of Jiangzhou; posthumous title Jing (Respectful).
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhenguan; posthumously named prefect of Jiangzhou and given the temple name Jing, "Respectful."

sentences.zh: 撰《開業平陳記》十一卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled Record of Founding the Enterprise and Pacifying Chen in eleven scrolls, circulated in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: He authored eleven fascicles of Record of the Founding and Pacification of Chen, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子宣機，高宗時官至銀青光祿大夫、太子左中護。

translations.literal: His son Xuanji, in the Gaozong reign reached office as Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Honors and Left Central Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanji rose under Gaozong to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Honors and Left Central Guard of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 宇文士及，雍州長安人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shiji, a man of Chang'an in Yong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shiji was a native of Chang'an in Yong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋右衛大將軍述子，化及弟也。

translations.literal: Son of Sui Right Guard General Shu, younger brother of Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of the Sui Right Guard General Yuwen Shu and younger brother of Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，以父勳封新城縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, by his father's merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Xincheng county.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era he was created Duke of Xincheng on his father's merit.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝嘗引入臥內，與語，奇之，令尚煬帝女南陽公主。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui once brought him into the sleeping quarters to converse, found him extraordinary, and ordered him to marry Emperor Yang's daughter, the Princess of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once received him in his private chamber, took to him, and had him marry Emperor Yang's daughter, the Princess of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 大業中，歷尚輦奉御，從幸江都。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he served successively as Imperial Carriage Attendant and followed on the journey of fortune to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daye he served as Imperial Carriage Attendant and accompanied the court to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起為鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's mourning, then was soon recalled as Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father but was soon recalled as Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations.

sentences.zh: 化及之潛謀逆亂也，以其主婿，深忌之而不告，既弒煬帝，署為內史令。

translations.literal: When Huaji secretly plotted rebellion, because he was the emperor's son-in-law Huaji deeply resented him and did not inform him; after killing Emperor Yang he appointed him Inner Scribe Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji plotted regicide he kept his brother-in-law in the dark out of deep suspicion; after murdering Emperor Yang he made him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖為殿內少監，時士及為奉御，深自結托。

translations.literal: Early on, when Gaozu was Vice Director of Palace Administration, at that time Shiji was an attendant and deeply bonded with him.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years, when Gaozu was Vice Director of Palace Administration, Shiji was an imperial attendant and formed a close bond with him.

sentences.zh: 及隨化及至黎陽，高祖手詔召之。

translations.literal: When he followed Huaji to Liyang, Gaozu with his own hand issued an edict summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Huaji to Liyang, Gaozu sent him a personal summons.

sentences.zh: 士及亦潛遣家僮間道詣長安申赤心，又因使密貢金環。

translations.literal: Shiji also secretly sent a household slave by bypaths to Chang'an to declare his loyal heart, and through an envoy secretly presented a gold ring.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji also sent a household servant by secret routes to Chang'an to pledge loyalty and, through an envoy, privately offered a gold ring.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，謂侍臣曰：「我與士及素經共事，今貢金環，是其來意也。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and told attendants: "I and Shiji long worked together; now he presents a gold ring—that is his meaning to come."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and told his ministers, "Shiji and I served together for years. This gold ring means he intends to come over."

sentences.zh: 」及至魏縣，兵威日蹙，士及勸之西歸長安，化及不從，士及乃與封倫求於濟北征督軍糧。

translations.literal: When they reached Wei county military prestige daily tightened; Shiji urged returning west to Chang'an; Huaji would not follow; Shiji then with Feng Lun requested at Jibei to levy and supervise army grain.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei county, with their forces failing, Shiji urged a march back to Chang'an; Huaji refused, and Shiji went with Feng Lun to Jibei on the pretext of collecting army grain.

sentences.zh: 俄而化及為竇建德所擒，濟北豪右多勸士及發青、齊之眾，北擊建德，收河北之地，以觀形勢。

translations.literal: Soon Huaji was captured by Dou Jiande; Jibei's powerful families mostly urged Shiji to raise the crowds of Qing and Qi, strike Jiande northward, recover Hebei lands, and observe how affairs stood.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huaji was taken by Dou Jiande; local magnates in Jibei urged Shiji to rally the forces of Qing and Qi, strike north against Jiande, and recover Hebei to test the balance of power.

sentences.zh: 士及不納，遂與封倫等來降。

translations.literal: Shiji did not accept and thereupon with Feng Lun and others came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji refused and surrendered with Feng Lun and the rest.

sentences.zh: 高祖數之曰：「汝兄弟率思歸之卒，為入關之計，當此之時，若得我父子，豈肯相存，今欲何地自處？

translations.literal: Gaozu reproached him, saying: "You brothers led troops longing to return and schemed to enter the passes; at that time, had you gotten me father and son, would you have spared us—now where do you wish to place yourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rebuked him: "You and your brother led men bent on entering the passes to seize power. Had you taken me and my son then, would you have let us live? Where do you mean to stand now?"

sentences.zh: 」士及謝曰：「臣之罪誠不容誅，但臣早奉龍顏，久存心腹，往在涿郡，嘗夜中密論時事，後於汾陰宮，復盡丹赤。

translations.literal: Shiji apologized, saying: "My crime indeed cannot bear not to be executed, but your servant early received the dragon countenance and long stored it in my heart; formerly at Zhuo commandery I once at midnight secretly discussed current affairs; later at the Fenyin palace again poured out my crimson loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji said, "My crimes deserve death, yet I long served Your Majesty in confidence—once at Zhuo commandery we spoke of affairs in secret at night, and again at Fenyin I poured out my loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自陛下龍飛九五，臣實傾心西歸，所以密申貢獻，冀此贖罪耳。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's dragon flight to the Ninety-Five, your servant truly bent my heart to return west; therefore I secretly declared offerings, hoping by this to redeem my crime.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne I have meant to come west; the gifts I sent were to prove my intent and atone."

sentences.zh: 」高祖笑謂裴寂曰：「此人與我言天下事，至今已六七年矣，公輩皆在其後。

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and said to Pei Ji: "This man has spoken with me of under-heaven affairs—it is already six or seven years; you gentlemen are all behind him."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and told Pei Ji, "He has discussed the realm with me for six or seven years already—you others came later."

sentences.zh: 」時士及妹為昭儀，有寵，由是漸見親待，授上儀同。

translations.literal: At the time Shiji's younger sister was a Brilliant Companion, with favor; thereby he gradually was seen and treated with intimacy, and given Senior Pillar of State parity.
translations.idiomatic: His sister was a favored imperial consort; he gradually won favor and was given the rank of Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 從太宗平宋金剛，以功復封新城縣公，妻以壽光縣主，仍遷秦王府驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Following Taizong he pacified Song Jingang; for merit he was again enfeoffed Duke of Xincheng, given in marriage the Princess of Shouguang county, and transferred to Swift Cavalry General of the Prince of Qin's house.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong against Song Jingang and was re-created Duke of Xincheng, married to a princess of Shouguang, and made Swift Cavalry General on the Prince of Qin's staff.

sentences.zh: 又從平王世充、竇建德，以功進爵郢國公，遷中書侍郎，再轉太子詹事。

translations.literal: Again he followed in pacifying Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande; for merit he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of E state, transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, then again turned to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande, was advanced to Duke of E, made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and later Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，代封倫為中書令，真食益州七百戶。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he replaced Feng Lun as Director of the Secretariat, with a substantive fief of seven hundred households in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded he replaced Feng Lun as Director of the Secretariat with a hereditary income of seven hundred households in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官檢校涼州都督。

translations.literal: Soon in his existing office he was supervising Commissioner of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting Commissioner of Liangzhou while retaining his central post.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為邊寇，士及欲立威以鎮邊服，每出入陳兵，盛為容衛；

translations.literal: At the time the Turks repeatedly raided the borders; Shiji wished to establish awe to calm the frontier submission; whenever he went in or out he arrayed troops and made grand his appearance guard;
translations.idiomatic: With Turks raiding the frontier, Shiji meant to awe them into submission; he marched with full escorts wherever he went,

sentences.zh: 又折節禮士，涼士服其威惠。

translations.literal: again he bent his bearing to honor scholar-gentry; Liang gentry submitted to his awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: yet humbled himself before local worthies, and the gentry of Liang admired both his force and his courtesy.

sentences.zh: 征為殿中監，以疾出為蒲州刺史，為政寬簡，吏人安之。

translations.literal: Summoned as Director of Palace Administration; on illness he went out as prefect of Pu, governing leniently and simply; clerks and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Director of Palace Administration, he was soon sent out as prefect of Pu on account of illness; his rule was easy and the people were content.

sentences.zh: 數歲，入為右衛大將軍，甚見親顧，每延入閣中，乙夜方出，遇其歸沐，仍遣馳召，同列莫與為比。

translations.literal: Several years later he entered as Right Guard General, greatly seen and favored; each time he was detained entering the inner pavilion and did not leave until the second watch; meeting his return-day bathing, still he was urgently summoned; among peers none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he became Right Guard General and enjoyed extraordinary favor—Taizong would keep him in the privy chamber until the second watch, and even on his bath days would send urgent summons; no colleague could match his standing.

sentences.zh: 然尤謹密，其妻每問向中使召有何樂事，士及終無所言。

translations.literal: Yet he was especially careful and secret; his wife often asked what pleasant matters the inner envoy's summons brought; Shiji to the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was exceedingly discreet; when his wife asked what affairs the palace called him for at night, he never told her.

sentences.zh: 尋錄其功，別封一子為新城縣公。

translations.literal: Soon his achievements were recorded and a separate son was enfeoffed Duke of Xincheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His merits were soon recognized and one of his sons was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 在職七年，復為殿中監，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In office seven years, again Director of Palace Administration, added Grand Master of Palace Honors with golden seal and violet ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in office he again became Director of Palace Administration and was given the rank of Grand Master with golden seal.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，太宗親問，撫之流涕。

translations.literal: When his illness was grave, Taizong personally inquired, stroked him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave Taizong visited him in person, stroked him, and wept.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十六年卒，贈左衛大將軍、涼州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan he died; posthumously Left Guard General and Commissioner of Liangzhou; buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenguan year sixteen, was posthumously named Left Guard General and Commissioner of Liangzhou, and was buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 士及撫幼弟及孤兄子，以友愛見稱，親戚故人貧乏者，輒遺之。

translations.literal: Shiji nurtured his young younger brother and orphaned elder brother's son, praised for brotherly love; relatives and old friends in poverty he would give to.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his young brother and orphaned nephews and was known for fraternal devotion; he gave freely to poor kin and old friends.

sentences.zh: 然厚自封植，衣食服玩必極奢侈。

translations.literal: Yet he thickly enriched himself; clothing, food, and curios must reach ultimate extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he enriched himself lavishly—his dress, food, and ornaments were always of the utmost extravagance.

sentences.zh: 謚曰「恭」，黃門侍郎劉洎駁之曰：「士及居家侈縱，不宜為恭。

translations.literal: Posthumous title "Gong" (Respectful); Yellow Gate Vice Director Liu Ji refuted it, saying: "Shiji at home was extravagant and unbridled—not fitting for Gong."
translations.idiomatic: He was first given the posthumous name Gong, "Respectful," but Vice Director Liu Ji objected: "Shiji lived in extravagance at home—Gong is not fitting."

sentences.zh: 」竟謚曰縱。

translations.literal: In the end the posthumous title was Zong (Unrestrained).
translations.idiomatic: The title was finally changed to Zong, "Unrestrained."

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：封倫多揣摩之才，有附托之巧。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Feng Lun had much talent for sizing up intent and skill in attaching himself to patrons.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Feng Lun had a genius for reading minds and a talent for attaching himself to power.

sentences.zh: 黨化及而數煬帝，或有赧顏；

translations.literal: He sided with Huaji yet counted off Emperor Yang—sometimes there was a flush of shame;
translations.idiomatic: He backed Huaji yet denounced Emperor Yang—sometimes with a flush of shame;

sentences.zh: 托士及以歸唐朝，殊無愧色。

translations.literal: he relied on Shiji to return to Tang—utterly without a blush.
translations.idiomatic: he rode Shiji's coattails back to Tang without the least embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 當建成之際，事持兩端；

translations.literal: At the time of Jiancheng he held to both ends of affairs;
translations.idiomatic: At the crisis over Jiancheng he straddled both sides;

sentences.zh: 背蕭瑀之恩，奏多異議。

translations.literal: he betrayed Xiao Yu's kindness and his memorials were full of dissent.
translations.idiomatic: he betrayed Xiao Yu's kindness and his memorials were full of dissent.

sentences.zh: 太宗，明主也，不見其心；

translations.literal: Taizong was a clear-sighted ruler yet did not see through him;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was a clear-sighted ruler yet did not see through him;

sentences.zh: 玄齡，賢相焉，尚容其諂。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling was a worthy chancellor yet still indulged his flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling was a worthy chancellor yet still indulged his flattery.

sentences.zh: 狡算醜行，死而後彰，苟非唐臨之劾，唐儉等議，則奸人得計矣。

translations.literal: His crafty schemes and ugly conduct were manifested only after death; if not for Tang Lin's impeachment and Tang Jian and others' deliberation, the villain would have had his way.
translations.idiomatic: His schemes and disgrace surfaced only after death; but for Tang Lin's impeachment and the debates of Tang Jian and others, the knave would have won out.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀骨鯁亮直，儒術清明。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu had bone-in-throat brightness and uprightness; Confucian learning clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu was fiercely upright, his Confucian learning lucid.

sentences.zh: 執政隋朝，忠而獲罪；

translations.literal: He held office under the Sui, loyal yet punished;
translations.idiomatic: He held office under the Sui, loyal yet punished;

sentences.zh: 委質高祖，知無不為。

translations.literal: he pledged himself to Gaozu and did everything he knew to do.
translations.idiomatic: he pledged himself to Gaozu and did everything he knew to do.

sentences.zh: 及太宗臨朝，房、杜用事，不容小過，欲居成功，既形猜貳之言，寧固或躍之位？

translations.literal: When Taizong held court, Fang and Du held affairs, tolerating no small fault; wishing to occupy success, already his words showed suspicion and division—how could he firmly hold a perch of leaping?
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, with Fang and Du in power and no slip forgiven, he still sought the top seat—his words already hinted at divided loyalty; could he cling to a place meant for contenders?

sentences.zh: 易名而祗加「褊」字，所幸者猶多；

translations.literal: Changing his posthumous name and only adding the character "narrow," what was fortunate still was still much;
translations.idiomatic: His name was changed to add only "narrow-minded"—he was still fortunate in that;

sentences.zh: 奉佛而不失道情，非善也而何謂。

translations.literal: honoring the Buddha without losing the feel of the Way—if not goodness, what would we call it?
translations.idiomatic: he served the Buddha without losing the moral temper of a gentleman—if that is not virtue, what is?

sentences.zh: 裴矩方略寬簡，士及通變謹密，皆一時之稱也。

translations.literal: Pei Ju had strategy and breadth with simplicity; Shiji had adaptive skill and careful secrecy—both were acclaimed of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju was strategic and magnanimous; Shiji adaptable and discreet—each was acclaimed in his day.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：封倫揣摩諂詐，蕭瑀骨鯁儒術。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Feng Lun sized up and flattered; Xiao Yu bone-in-throat Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Feng Lun read minds and flattered; Xiao Yu upright and learned in Confucian tradition.

sentences.zh: 裴矩方略寬簡，士及通變謹密。

translations.literal: Pei Ju: strategy broad and simple; Shiji: adaptive skill, careful secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju—strategic and magnanimous; Shiji—adaptable and discreet.
